title.raw: 卷一百十四 列傳第二 后妃二 Volume 114 Biographies 2: Empresses and Consorts 2

sentences.zh: 孝宗孝康張皇后 武宗孝靜夏皇后 世宗孝潔陳皇后 張廢后 孝烈方皇后 孝恪杜太后 穆宗孝懿李皇后 孝安陳皇后 孝定李太后 神宗孝端王皇后 劉昭妃 孝靖王太后 鄭貴妃 光宗孝元郭皇后 孝和王太后 孝純劉太后 李康妃 李莊妃 趙選侍 熹宗懿安張皇后 張裕妃 莊烈帝愍周皇后 田貴妃

translations.literal: Empress Zhang the Xiaokang of Emperor Xiaozong; Empress Xia the Xiaojing of Emperor Wuzong; Empress Chen the Xiaojie of Emperor Shizong; the deposed Empress Zhang; Empress Fang the Xiaolie; Empress Dowager Du the Xiaoke; Empress Li the Xiaoyi of Emperor Muzong; Empress Chen the Xiao'an; Empress Dowager Li the Xiaoding; Empress Wang the Xiaoduan of Emperor Shenzong; Consort Liu the Zhaohui; Empress Dowager Wang the Xiaojing; Noble Consort Zheng; Empress Guo the Xiaoyuan of Emperor Guangzong; Empress Dowager Wang the Xiaohe; Empress Dowager Liu the Xiaochun; Imperial Concubine Li Kang; Imperial Concubine Li Zhuang; Selected Attendant Zhao; Empress Zhang the Yi'an of Emperor Xizong; Imperial Concubine Zhang Yu; Empress Zhou the Min of the Chonglie Emperor; Noble Consort Tian.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhang (posthumous name Xiaokang), consort of Emperor Xiaozong; Empress Xia (Xiaojing), consort of Emperor Wuzong; Empress Chen (Xiaojie), consort of Emperor Shizong; the deposed Empress Zhang; Empress Fang (Xiaolie); Empress Dowager Du (Xiaoke); Empress Li (Xiaoyi), consort of Emperor Muzong; Empress Chen (Xiao'an); Empress Dowager Li (Xiaoding); Empress Wang (Xiaoduan), consort of Emperor Shenzong; Consort Liu (Zhaohui); Empress Dowager Wang (Xiaojing); Noble Consort Zheng; Empress Guo (Xiaoyuan), consort of Emperor Guangzong; Empress Dowager Wang (Xiaohe); Empress Dowager Liu (Xiaochun); Imperial Concubine Li Kang; Imperial Concubine Li Zhuang; Selected Attendant Zhao; Empress Zhang (Yi'an), consort of Emperor Xizong; Imperial Concubine Zhang Yu; Empress Zhou (Min), consort of the Chongzhen Emperor; Noble Consort Tian.

sentences.zh: 孝宗孝康皇后張氏，興濟人。

translations.literal: Empress Zhang the Xiaokang of Emperor Xiaozong was a native of Xingji.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhang, known posthumously as Xiaokang and consort of Emperor Xiaozong, came from Xingji.

sentences.zh: 父巒，以鄉貢入太學。

translations.literal: Her father Luan entered the Imperial University through the local tribute examination.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Luan had entered the Imperial University as a tribute scholar from the provinces.

sentences.zh: 母金氏，夢月入懷而生后。

translations.literal: Her mother was of the Jin clan; she dreamed that the moon entered her bosom and thereafter gave birth to the future empress.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother, née Jin, dreamed that the moon entered her womb, and afterward bore the future empress.

sentences.zh: 成化二十三年選為太子妃。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Chenghua she was chosen as crown prince's consort.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year of the Chenghua reign she was selected to be crown prince's consort.

sentences.zh: 是年，孝宗即位，冊立為皇后。

translations.literal: That year, when Xiaozong took the throne, she was invested as empress.
translations.idiomatic: The same year, when Emperor Xiaozong ascended the throne, she was formally installed as empress.

sentences.zh: 帝頗優禮外家，追封巒昌國公，封后弟鶴齡壽寧侯，延齡建昌伯，為后立家廟於興濟，工作壯麗，數年始畢。

translations.literal: The emperor treated her maiden family with great favor: Luan was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Chang; her younger brothers Heling and Yanling were made Marquis of Shouning and Baron of Jianchang respectively; a family temple was built for the empress at Xingji, magnificently constructed over several years before it was finished.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor lavished favors on her kin: Luan was posthumously made Duke of Chang; her brothers Heling and Yanling became Marquis of Shouning and Baron of Jianchang; a family temple for the empress was raised at Xingji on a grand scale and took years to complete.

sentences.zh: 鶴齡、延齡並註籍宮禁，縱家人為奸利，中外諸臣多以為言，帝以后故不問。

translations.literal: Heling and Yanling were both registered in the palace rolls and allowed their households to pursue illicit profit; officials at court and beyond repeatedly remonstrated, but the emperor ignored it for the empress's sake.
translations.idiomatic: Heling and Yanling were entered on the palace register and let their households profit by fraud; ministers inside and outside the court spoke out repeatedly, yet the emperor took no action out of regard for the empress.

sentences.zh: 武宗即位，尊為皇太后。

translations.literal: When Wuzong took the throne, she was honored as empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wuzong came to the throne, she was honored as empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 五年十二月，以寘鐇平，上尊號曰慈壽皇太后。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the fifth year, because the rebellion of Prince of An was pacified, she was given the honorific title Empress Dowager Cishou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of his fifth year, after the pacification of Prince of An's rebellion, she received the elevated title Empress Dowager Cishou.

sentences.zh: 世宗入繼，稱聖母，加上尊號曰「昭聖慈壽」。

translations.literal: When Shizong succeeded to the throne, she was called Holy Mother, and the honorific title "Zhaosheng Cishou" was added.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong inherited the throne, she was styled Holy Mother, with the added honorific "Zhaosheng Cishou."

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三年加上「昭聖康惠慈壽」。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiajing "Zhaosheng Kanghui Cishou" was added.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jiajing the title was further extended to "Zhaosheng Kanghui Cishou."

sentences.zh: 已，改稱伯母。

translations.literal: Thereafter she was redesignated aunt.
translations.idiomatic: Later she was addressed instead as the emperor's aunt.

sentences.zh: 十五年復加上「昭聖恭安康惠慈壽」。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year "Zhaosheng Gong'an Kanghui Cishou" was again added.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year the honorific was expanded again to "Zhaosheng Gong'an Kanghui Cishou."

sentences.zh: 二十年八月崩，諡曰「孝康靖肅莊慈哲懿翊天贊聖敬皇后」，合葬泰陵，祔廟。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the twentieth year she died; her posthumous title was "Empress Xiaokang Jingsu Zhuangci Zheyi Yitian Zansheng Jing"; she was buried with the emperor at Tailing and enshrined in the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: She died in the eighth month of the twentieth year and was given the posthumous title Empress Xiaokang Jingsu Zhuangci Zheyi Yitian Zansheng Jing; she was interred with the emperor at Tailing and received temple enshrinement.

sentences.zh: 初，興國太后以籓妃入，太后猶以故事遇之，帝頗不悅。

translations.literal: At first, when the Empress Dowager of Xingguo entered the palace as a prince's consort, the empress dowager still treated her according to old precedent, which greatly displeased the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Early on, when the Empress Dowager of Xingguo arrived at court as a prince's wife, Empress Dowager Zhang still dealt with her by the old rules of precedence, and the emperor took strong offense.

sentences.zh: 及帝朝，太后待之又倨。

translations.literal: When the emperor came to court, the empress dowager treated her again with arrogance.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor attended court, the empress dowager treated her with renewed haughtiness.

sentences.zh: 會太后弟延齡為人所告，帝坐延齡謀逆論死，太后窘迫無所出。

translations.literal: When the empress dowager's younger brother Yanling was denounced by someone, the emperor convicted Yanling of plotting rebellion and sentenced him to death; the empress dowager was cornered and had no recourse.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanling, the empress dowager's brother, was accused, the emperor found him guilty of treason and condemned him to death; the empress dowager was trapped and could see no way out.

sentences.zh: 哀衝太子生，請入賀，帝謝不見。

translations.literal: When the Aichong heir apparent was born, she asked to enter and offer congratulations; the emperor declined and would not see her.
translations.idiomatic: At the birth of the heir apparent Aichong, she requested an audience to offer congratulations, but the emperor refused to receive her.

sentences.zh: 使人請，不許。

translations.literal: She sent someone to request again; permission was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: She sent envoys to ask again, but he would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 大學士張孚敬亦為延齡請，帝手敕曰：「天下者，高皇帝之天下，孝宗皇帝守高皇帝法。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Zhang Fuling also pleaded for Yanling; the emperor wrote in his own hand: "The realm belongs to the Founding Emperor; Emperor Xiaozong upheld the Founding Emperor's law.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Zhang Fuling also interceded for Yanling; the emperor replied in his own hand: "The realm belongs to the Founding Emperor, and Emperor Xiaozong upheld the Founding Emperor's law.

sentences.zh: 卿慮傷伯母心，豈不慮傷高、孝二廟心耶？

translations.literal: You worry about wounding your aunt's heart—do you not worry about wounding the hearts of the Founding Emperor and Xiaozong in their temples?
translations.idiomatic: You fret over hurting your aunt's feelings—do you not fret over hurting the Founding Emperor and Emperor Xiaozong in their ancestral shrines?

sentences.zh: 」孚敬復奏曰：「陛下嗣位時，用臣言，稱伯母皇太后，朝臣歸過陛下，至今未已。

translations.literal: " Fuling memorialized again: "When Your Majesty succeeded to the throne, you followed my advice and called her Aunt Empress Dowager; the court officials blamed Your Majesty, and that has not ceased to this day.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhang Fuling memorialized again: "When Your Majesty first took the throne, you followed my counsel and styled her Aunt Empress Dowager; the court blamed Your Majesty then, and has not stopped since.

sentences.zh: 茲者大小臣工默無一言，誠幸太后不得令終，以重陛下過耳。

translations.literal: Now great and small officials are silent without a word, truly hoping the empress dowager will not meet a good end, so as to deepen Your Majesty's fault.
translations.idiomatic: Now ministers high and low say nothing at all—they would almost welcome the empress dowager's dishonorable end, the better to magnify Your Majesty's blame.

sentences.zh: 夫謀逆之罪，獄成當坐族誅，昭聖獨非張氏乎？

translations.literal: The crime of plotting rebellion, once the case is closed, calls for execution of the entire clan—is the Zhaosheng alone not of the Zhang clan?
translations.idiomatic: Treason, once proved, demands the extermination of the whole clan—is Empress Dowager Zhaosheng not herself a Zhang?

sentences.zh: 陛下何以處此！

translations.literal: How will Your Majesty deal with this!
translations.idiomatic: How can Your Majesty resolve this!

sentences.zh: 」冬月慮囚，帝又欲殺延齡，復以孚敬言而止。

translations.literal: " In the winter month of reviewing prisoners, the emperor again wished to execute Yanling, but again stopped on Fuling's words.
translations.idiomatic: " During the winter review of prisoners, the emperor again meant to put Yanling to death, but once more held back on Zhang Fuling's plea.

sentences.zh: 亡何，奸人劉東山者告變，並逮鶴齡下詔獄。

translations.literal: Before long, a villain named Liu Dongshan reported a plot, and Heling was also seized and sent to the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward a schemer named Liu Dongshan denounced a conspiracy, and Heling too was arrested and thrown into the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 太后至衣敝襦席藁為請，亦不聽。

translations.literal: The empress dowager went so far as to wear tattered clothes and sit on straw matting to plead, but he still would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager humbled herself in worn garments on a straw mat to beg for mercy, yet he would not heed her.

sentences.zh: 久之，鶴齡瘐死。

translations.literal: After a long while, Heling died of illness in prison.
translations.idiomatic: In time Heling died of illness in custody.

sentences.zh: 及太后崩，帝竟殺延齡，事詳《外戚傳》。

translations.literal: When the empress dowager died, the emperor at last executed Yanling; the matter is detailed in the "Biographies of Imperial Affines."
translations.idiomatic: After the empress dowager's death, the emperor finally had Yanling executed; the full account appears in the Biographies of Imperial Affines.

sentences.zh: 武宗孝靜皇后夏氏，上元人。

translations.literal: Empress Xia the Xiaojing of Emperor Wuzong, née Xia, was a native of Shangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xia, posthumous name Xiaojing and consort of Emperor Wuzong, came from Shangyuan.

sentences.zh: 正德元年冊立為皇后。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengde she was invested as empress.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Zhengde reign she was formally made empress.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖元年上尊稱曰「莊肅皇后」。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiajing she was given the honorific title "Empress Zhuangsu."
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jiajing she received the elevated title Empress Zhuangsu.

sentences.zh: 十四年正月崩，合葬康陵，祔廟。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourteenth year she died; she was buried with the emperor at Kangling and enshrined in the temple.
translations.idiomatic: She died in the first month of the fourteenth year, was interred with the emperor at Kangling, and enshrined in the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 初，禮臣上喪儀，帝曰：「嫂叔無服，且兩宮在上，朕服青，臣民如母后服。

translations.literal: At first, when the ritual officials presented mourning rites, the emperor said: "Between sister-in-law and brother-in-law there is no mourning garment; moreover, with both palaces above, I shall wear green, and officials and people shall mourn as for an empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: When the ritual officials first proposed funeral observances, the emperor said: "A brother-in-law owes no mourning dress to a sister-in-law; with both empress dowagers still living, I shall wear green, while officials and commoners shall observe mourning as for an empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 」禮部尚書夏言曰：「皇上以嫂叔絕服，則群臣不敢素服見皇上，請暫罷朝參。

translations.literal: " Minister of Rites Xia Yan said: "If Your Majesty, citing the rule that sister-in-law and brother-in-law do not mourn one another, will not wear white, then the assembled ministers dare not appear before Your Majesty in white; we ask that court audiences be suspended for the time being.
translations.idiomatic: " Minister of Rites Xia Yan replied: "If Your Majesty, invoking the exemption between sister-in-law and brother-in-law, refuses white mourning, the ministers cannot attend court in white; we beg that audiences be suspended for now.

sentences.zh: 」許之。

translations.literal: " Permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 已而議諡，大學士張孚敬曰：「大行皇后，上嫂也，與累朝元后異，宜用二字或四字。

translations.literal: Thereafter, when posthumous titles were debated, Grand Secretary Zhang Fuling said: "The late empress was Your Majesty's sister-in-law, unlike the primary empresses of successive reigns; a title of two or four characters should be used.
translations.idiomatic: When the posthumous title was debated, Grand Secretary Zhang Fuling argued: "The late empress was Your Majesty's sister-in-law, not a primary empress of earlier reigns; two or four characters would suffice.

sentences.zh: 」李時曰：「宜用八。

translations.literal: " Li Shi said: "Eight should be used.
translations.idiomatic: " Li Shi held that eight characters were appropriate.

sentences.zh: 」左都御史王廷相、吏部侍郎霍韜等曰：「均帝后也，何殊！

translations.literal: " Censor-in-Chief Wang Tingxiang, Vice Minister of Personnel Huo Tao, and others said: "All are imperial consorts—what difference is there!
translations.idiomatic: " Censor-in-Chief Wang Tingxiang, Vice Minister Huo Tao, and others protested: "She was still the emperor's consort—why treat her differently!

sentences.zh: 」言集眾議，因奏曰：「古人尚質，諡法簡，稱其行，後人增加，臣子情也。

translations.literal: " Yan gathered collective opinion and memorialized: "The ancients valued simplicity; posthumous titles were brief, naming their conduct; later generations added characters—this is the feeling of subjects.
translations.idiomatic: " Xia Yan collected opinions and memorialized: "Antiquity favored simplicity in posthumous titles; later ages lengthened them out of loyal affection—that is all.

sentences.zh: 生今世，宜行今制。

translations.literal: Living in the present age, the present system should be followed.
translations.idiomatic: We live in the present and should follow present practice.

sentences.zh: 大行皇后宜如列聖元后諡，二四及八，於禮無據。

translations.literal: The late empress should receive a posthumous title like the primary empresses of successive sage emperors; two, four, or eight characters have no basis in ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The late empress deserves the same style of posthumous title as primary empresses of past reigns; two, four, or eight characters lack ritual warrant.

sentences.zh: 」帝不從，命再議。

translations.literal: " The emperor did not agree and ordered further deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor refused and ordered the matter debated again.

sentences.zh: 群臣請如孚敬言。

translations.literal: The assembled ministers asked to follow Fuling's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers asked to follow Zhang Fuling's recommendation.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「用六，合陰數焉。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Use six—it accords with the yin number.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Use six characters—it suits the yin number.

sentences.zh: 」於是上諡「孝靜莊惠安肅毅皇后」。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the posthumous title "Empress Xiaojing Zhuanghui Ansu Yi" was bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: " She was then given the posthumous title Empress Xiaojing Zhuanghui Ansu Yi.

sentences.zh: 十五年，帝覺孚敬言非是，敕曰：「孝靜皇后諡不備，不稱配武宗。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year the emperor perceived that Fuling's words had been wrong and issued an edict: "Empress Xiaojing's posthumous title is incomplete and unworthy of her as consort of Wuzong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year the emperor decided Zhang Fuling had been mistaken and decreed: "Empress Xiaojing's posthumous title is inadequate and does not honor her as consort of Emperor Wuzong.

sentences.zh: 」乃改諡「孝靜莊惠安肅溫誠順天偕聖毅皇后」。

translations.literal: " The title was then changed to "Empress Xiaojing Zhuanghui Ansu Wencheng Shuntian Xiesheng Yi."
translations.idiomatic: " It was revised to Empress Xiaojing Zhuanghui Ansu Wencheng Shuntian Xiesheng Yi.

sentences.zh: 孝烈皇后方氏，世宗第三后也，江寧人。

translations.literal: Empress Fang the Xiaolie was the third empress of Shizong and a native of Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Fang, posthumous name Xiaolie, was Emperor Shizong's third empress and came from Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 帝即位且十年，未有子。

translations.literal: The emperor had been on the throne nearly ten years without a son.
translations.idiomatic: Nearly ten years into his reign the emperor still had no son.

sentences.zh: 大學士張孚敬言：「古者天子立后，並建六宮、三夫人、九嬪、二十七世婦、八十一御妻，所以廣嗣也。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Zhang Fuling said: "In antiquity, when the Son of Heaven installed an empress, he also established the six palaces, three ladies, nine consorts, twenty-seven attendant ladies, and eighty-one royal wives, thereby to broaden the succession.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Zhang Fuling urged: "In antiquity the Son of Heaven, on installing an empress, also filled the six palaces with three ladies, nine consorts, twenty-seven attendant ladies, and eighty-one royal wives—to secure the succession.

sentences.zh: 陛下春秋鼎盛，宜博求淑女，為子嗣計。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is in the prime of life and should widely seek virtuous ladies for the sake of heirs.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is in his prime; he should seek virtuous ladies widely for the sake of an heir.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " The proposal was followed.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 十年三月，后與鄭氏、王氏、閻氏、韋氏、沈氏、盧氏、沈氏、杜氏同冊為九嬪，冠九翟冠，大採鞠衣，圭用次玉，谷文，冊黃金塗，視皇后殺五分之一。

translations.literal: In the third month of the tenth year, the future empress together with the Zheng, Wang, Yan, Wei, Shen, Lu, Shen, and Du clans were all invested as nine consorts; they wore the nine-pheasant crown and great ceremonial robes of many colors; their scepters used secondary jade with grain pattern; their investiture books were gold-plated; their insignia were one-fifth less than the empress's.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the tenth year she was invested together with ladies Zheng, Wang, Yan, Wei, Shen, Lu, Shen, and Du as nine consorts, wearing the nine-pheasant crown and full ceremonial dress, with secondary jade scepters and gold-plated investiture scrolls, their regalia one-fifth below the empress's.

sentences.zh: 至期，帝袞冕告太廟，還服皮弁，御華蓋殿，傳制，遣大臣行冊禮。

translations.literal: When the day came, the emperor in full regalia announced to the Grand Temple, then changed to the leather cap, took the throne at the Huagai Hall, issued the decree, and dispatched great ministers to perform the investiture rites.
translations.idiomatic: On the appointed day the emperor, in full ceremonial dress, reported to the Grand Temple, then changed to the leather cap, presided at Huagai Hall, issued the decree, and sent senior ministers to conduct the investiture.

sentences.zh: 既冊​​，從皇后朝奉先殿。

translations.literal: After investiture, she followed the empress in audience at the Hall of Imperial Ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: After investiture she accompanied the empress in paying court at the Hall of Imperial Ancestors.

sentences.zh: 禮成，帝服皮弁，受百官賀，蓋創禮也。

translations.literal: When the rites were complete, the emperor in the leather cap received congratulations from the hundred officials—this was a newly created ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites ended, the emperor in the leather cap received congratulations from all officials—a ceremony invented for the occasion.

sentences.zh: 張后廢，遂立為后，而封沈氏為宸妃，閻氏為麗妃。

translations.literal: When Empress Zhang was deposed, Fang was then installed as empress, while Lady Shen was enfeoffed as Chen consort and Lady Yan as Li consort.
translations.idiomatic: After Empress Zhang was deposed, Fang was made empress; Lady Shen became Chen consort and Lady Yan Li consort.

sentences.zh: 舊制：立后，謁內廟而已。

translations.literal: By old regulation, on installing an empress one paid homage only at the inner temple.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly, installing an empress required homage only at the inner temple.

sentences.zh: 至是，下禮臣議廟見禮。

translations.literal: On this occasion the emperor ordered ritual officials to deliberate the temple-audience rites.
translations.idiomatic: Now he ordered the ritual officials to draft rites for the empress's temple audience.

sentences.zh: 於是群臣以天子立三宮以承宗廟，《禮經》有廟見之文，乃考據《禮經》，參稽《大明集禮》，擬儀注以上。

translations.literal: Thereupon the ministers cited that the Son of Heaven establishes the three palaces to sustain the ancestral temple, and that the Book of Rites contains passages on temple audience; they researched the Book of Rites, consulted the Collected Rites of the Great Ming, and drafted ritual protocols for submission.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers argued that the Son of Heaven fills the three palaces to sustain the ancestral cult and that the Book of Rites prescribes a temple audience; they studied the classics and the Collected Rites of the Great Ming and submitted a draft protocol.

sentences.zh: 至期，帝率后謁太廟及世廟。

translations.literal: When the day came, the emperor led the empress to pay homage at the Grand Temple and the Imperial Lineage Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On the appointed day the emperor led the empress to the Grand Temple and the lineage temple.

sentences.zh: 越三日，頒詔天下。

translations.literal: Three days later an edict was promulgated throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later an edict went out to the whole empire.

sentences.zh: 明日，受命婦朝。

translations.literal: The next day, titled ladies came to court in audience.
translations.idiomatic: The following day titled ladies attended court in audience.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，宮婢楊金英等謀弒逆，帝賴后救得免，乃進后父泰和伯銳爵為侯。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, palace maidservants Yang Jinying and others plotted regicide; the emperor escaped only because the empress saved him, whereupon her father Rui, Baron of Taihe, was promoted to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year palace maids led by Yang Jinying plotted to assassinate the emperor; he survived only because the empress rescued him, and her father Rui, Baron of Taihe, was raised to marquis.

sentences.zh: 初，曹妃有色，帝愛之，冊為端妃。

translations.literal: At first Consort Cao was beautiful and the emperor favored her; she was invested as Duan consort.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Cao was beautiful and greatly favored; she was made Duan consort.

sentences.zh: 是夕，帝宿端妃宮。

translations.literal: That evening the emperor lodged in Consort Duan's palace.
translations.idiomatic: That night the emperor slept in Consort Duan's quarters.

sentences.zh: 金英等伺帝熟寢，以組縊帝項，誤為死結，得不絕。

translations.literal: Jinying and the others waited until the emperor was fast asleep, then strangled his neck with a cord; by mistake they tied a dead knot, so he did not suffocate.
translations.idiomatic: Jinying and her accomplices waited until the emperor was deep asleep, then looped a cord about his neck; they tied a knot that would not tighten, and he did not die.

sentences.zh: 同事張金蓮知事不就，走告后。

translations.literal: Her accomplice Zhang Jinlian, seeing the plot would not succeed, ran to inform the empress.
translations.idiomatic: Their accomplice Zhang Jinlian, seeing the plot fail, ran to warn the empress.

sentences.zh: 后馳至，解組，帝蘇。

translations.literal: The empress rushed there, untied the cord, and the emperor revived.
translations.idiomatic: The empress hurried in, loosened the cord, and the emperor came to.

sentences.zh: 后命內監張佐等捕宮人雜治，言金英等弒逆，王寧嬪首謀。

translations.literal: The empress ordered the eunuch Zhang Zuo and others to seize palace women and torture them indiscriminately, declaring that Jinying and others had attempted regicide and that Lady Wang, the Ning consort, was the chief plotter.
translations.idiomatic: She ordered the eunuch Zhang Zuo and others to seize palace women and torture them at random, alleging that Jinying's party had attempted regicide and that Consort Wang Ning was the ringleader.

sentences.zh: 又曰：曹端妃雖不與，亦知謀。

translations.literal: She also said: "Though Consort Cao Duan did not take part, she knew of the plot."
translations.idiomatic: She also claimed that although Consort Cao Duan had not joined the plot, she had known of it.

sentences.zh: 時帝病悸不能言，后傳帝命收端妃、寧嬪及金英等悉礫於市。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor was ill with palpitations and could not speak; the empress transmitted the imperial command to arrest Consort Duan, Consort Ning, and Jinying and the rest, all of whom were dismembered in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was shaken and speechless; the empress issued orders in his name to seize Consort Duan, Consort Ning, Jinying, and the rest, who were all torn apart in the public square.

sentences.zh: 並誅其族屬十餘人。

translations.literal: More than ten of their clansmen were also executed.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten of their kinsmen were put to death as well.

sentences.zh: 然妃實不知也。

translations.literal: Yet the consort in fact knew nothing of it.
translations.idiomatic: In truth the consort had known nothing of the plot.

sentences.zh: 久之，帝始知其冤。

translations.literal: After a long while the emperor came to know her wrongful death.
translations.idiomatic: Only much later did the emperor learn she had been innocent.

sentences.zh: 二十六年十一月乙未，后崩。

translations.literal: On the yimwei day of the eleventh month of the twenty-sixth year the empress died.
translations.idiomatic: On the yimwei day of the eleventh month of the twenty-sixth year the empress died.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「皇后比救朕危，奉天濟難，其以元后禮葬。

translations.literal: An edict said: "The empress lately saved Us from peril and aided Heaven in relieving calamity; let her be buried with the rites of a primary empress.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "The empress lately saved Us from peril and aided Heaven in our distress; bury her with the rites due a primary empress.

sentences.zh: 」預名葬地曰「永陵」，諡孝烈，親定諡禮，視昔加隆焉。

translations.literal: " The burial site was beforehand named "Yongling"; her posthumous title was Xiaolie; the emperor personally fixed the posthumous rites, more exalted than in former times.
translations.idiomatic: " Her tomb was named Yongling in advance; she received the posthumous title Xiaolie; the emperor personally set the funeral rites, more lavish than before.

sentences.zh: 禮成，頒詔天下。

translations.literal: When the rites were complete, an edict was promulgated throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites were finished, an edict went out to the whole empire.

sentences.zh: 及大祥，禮臣請安主奉先殿東夾室，帝曰：「奉先殿夾室，非正也，可即祔太廟。

translations.literal: At the end of the second year of mourning, ritual officials asked to install her spirit tablet in the eastern side chamber of the Hall of Imperial Ancestors; the emperor said: "A side chamber of the Hall of Imperial Ancestors is not the proper place; she may be enshrined directly in the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the mourning period ritual officials proposed placing her tablet in the eastern side chamber of the Hall of Imperial Ancestors; the emperor said: "A side chamber there is improper—enshrine her at once in the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 」於是大學士嚴嵩等請設位於太廟東，皇妣睿皇后之次，后寢藏主則設幄於憲廟皇祖妣之右，以從祔於祖姑之義。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Grand Secretary Yan Song and others asked to set her place on the east of the Grand Temple, next after the emperor's mother Empress Rui; when the empress's resting hall stored the tablet, a canopy would be set on the right of the imperial ancestress in the Xian Temple, following the principle of enshrinement with a husband's paternal aunt.
translations.idiomatic: " Grand Secretary Yan Song and others proposed a place in the eastern wing of the Grand Temple after Empress Rui, with a canopy in the Xian Temple to the right of the imperial ancestress, following the rite of enshrinement with a husband's paternal aunt.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「祔禮至重，豈可權就。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Enshrinement rites are of the utmost weight—how can they be settled provisionally?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "Enshrinement is too weighty a matter to settle by expedient.

sentences.zh: 后非帝，乃配帝者，自有一定之序，安有享從此而主藏彼之禮！

translations.literal: The empress is not an emperor but one who shares the emperor's shrine—there is a fixed order of precedence; how can there be a rite of offering sacrifice here while storing the tablet there!
translations.idiomatic: An empress is not an emperor but one who shares his shrine—there is a fixed order; what rite offers sacrifice in one place while keeping the tablet in another!

sentences.zh: 其祧仁宗，祔以新序，即朕位次，勿得亂禮。

translations.literal: Remove Renzong from the temple and enshrine her in the new order—that is, in Our own place in the sequence; do not disturb the rites.
translations.idiomatic: Remove Emperor Renzong from the temple and enshrine her in the new order—at Our own place in the sequence; do not confuse the rites.

sentences.zh: 」嵩曰：「祔新序，非臣下所敢言，且陰不可當陽位。

translations.literal: " Song said: "Enshrinement in the new order is not something subjects dare propose; moreover, yin cannot occupy yang's place.
translations.idiomatic: " Yan Song objected: "Subjects dare not propose a new order of enshrinement; moreover, yin cannot take yang's place.

sentences.zh: 」乃命姑藏主睿皇后側。

translations.literal: " He was ordered for the time being to store the tablet beside Empress Rui.
translations.idiomatic: " For the present he was told to place the tablet beside Empress Rui.

sentences.zh: 二十九年十月，帝終欲祔后太廟，命再議。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the twenty-ninth year the emperor at last wished to enshrine the empress in the Grand Temple and ordered further deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the twenty-ninth year the emperor still meant to enshrine her in the Grand Temple and ordered the matter debated again.

sentences.zh: 尚書徐階言不可，給事中楊思忠是階議，餘無言者。

translations.literal: Minister Xu Jie said it could not be done; supervising secretary Yang Sizhong agreed with Xu's view; the rest were silent.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Xu Jie argued against it; supervising secretary Yang Sizhong sided with Xu; no one else spoke.

sentences.zh: 帝覘知狀。

translations.literal: The emperor perceived how matters stood.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw how the court stood.

sentences.zh: 及議疏入，謂：「后正位中宮，禮宜祔享，但遽及廟次，則臣子之情，不唯不敢，實不忍也。

translations.literal: When the deliberation memorial came in, it said: "The empress held the central palace in rightful standing and should by rite receive enshrinement and sacrifice, but to rush to alter the temple order—subjects' feeling is not only that they dare not, they truly cannot bear it.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, it read: "The empress rightly held the central palace and deserves enshrinement, but to alter the temple order so hastily—your subjects not only dare not, they truly cannot bear it.

sentences.zh: 宜設位奉先殿。

translations.literal: A place should be set in the Hall of Imperial Ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: Set her place in the Hall of Imperial Ancestors instead.

sentences.zh: 」帝震怒。

translations.literal: " The emperor was greatly enraged.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor flew into a rage.

sentences.zh: 階、思忠惶恐言：「周建九廟，三昭三穆。

translations.literal: Xu and Yang said in alarm: "The Zhou established nine temples with three zhao and three mu.
translations.idiomatic: Xu and Yang said in alarm: "The Zhou built nine temples with three zhao and three mu.

sentences.zh: 國朝廟制，同堂異室，與《周禮》不同。

translations.literal: Our dynasty's temple system uses one hall with separate chambers, differing from the Rites of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty's temples share one hall with separate chambers, unlike the Rites of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 今太廟九室皆滿，若以聖躬論，仁宗當祧，固不待言，但此乃異日聖子神孫之事。

translations.literal: Now all nine chambers of the Grand Temple are full; if one considers Your Majesty's person, Renzong should be removed from the temple—this goes without saying—but that is a matter for sage sons and divine grandsons on another day.
translations.idiomatic: All nine chambers of the Grand Temple are full; for Your Majesty's sake Renzong ought to be removed—that goes without saying—but that is for sage sons and grandsons on another day.

sentences.zh: 臣聞夏人之廟五，商以七，周以九。

translations.literal: Your subjects have heard that the Xia had five temples, the Shang seven, and the Zhou nine.
translations.idiomatic: We are told the Xia kept five temples, the Shang seven, and the Zhou nine.

sentences.zh: 禮由義起，五可七，七可九，九之外亦可加也。

translations.literal: Rites arise from principle: five may become seven, seven nine, and beyond nine one may also add.
translations.idiomatic: Rites follow principle—five may become seven, seven nine, and beyond nine more may be added.

sentences.zh: 請於太廟及奉先殿各增二室，以祔孝烈，則仁宗可不必祧，孝烈皇后可速正南面之位，陛下亦無預祧以俟之嫌。

translations.literal: We request adding two chambers each to the Grand Temple and the Hall of Imperial Ancestors to enshrine Xiaolie—then Renzong need not be removed from the temple, Empress Xiaolie can quickly assume the position facing south, and Your Majesty will also have no suspicion of pre-emptively removing an ancestor to wait.
translations.idiomatic: Add two chambers each to the Grand Temple and the Hall of Imperial Ancestors to enshrine Xiaolie, and Renzong need not be removed; Empress Xiaolie can at once take her rightful place facing south, and Your Majesty avoids any appearance of removing an ancestor in advance.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「臣子之誼，當祧當祔，力請可也。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "In the duty of minister and subject, when one should remove or enshrine, it is fitting to plead forcefully.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said: "As subjects, when removal or enshrinement is called for, you may press your case as hard as you like.

sentences.zh: 苟禮得其正，何避豫為！

translations.literal: If the rites achieve what is correct, why avoid acting in advance!
translations.idiomatic: If the rites are truly right, why shrink from acting now!

sentences.zh: 」於是階等複會廷臣上言：「唐、虞、夏五廟，其祀皆止四世。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Xu and the others again gathered court officials and memorialized: "The Tang, Yu, and Xia had five temples; their sacrifices all stopped at four generations.
translations.idiomatic: " Xu and his colleagues then reconvened the court and memorialized: "The Tang, Yu, and Xia kept five temples, and their sacrifices reached only four generations.

sentences.zh: 周九廟，三昭三穆，然而兄弟相及，亦不能盡足六世。

translations.literal: The Zhou had nine temples, three zhao and three mu, yet even with brothers succeeding one another, six generations could not be fully accommodated.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou built nine temples with three zhao and three mu, yet even when brothers succeeded one another, six generations could not all be housed.

sentences.zh: 今仁宗為皇上五世祖，以聖躬論，仁宗於禮當祧，孝烈皇后於禮當祔。

translations.literal: Now Renzong is Your Majesty's five-generation ancestor; considering Your Majesty's person, Renzong should by rite be removed from the temple, and Empress Xiaolie should by rite be enshrined.
translations.idiomatic: Renzong is now Your Majesty's five-generation ancestor; on Your Majesty's account Renzong ought by rite to be removed, and Empress Xiaolie ought by rite to be enshrined.

sentences.zh: 請祧仁宗，祔孝烈皇后於太廟第九室。

translations.literal: We request removing Renzong and enshrining Empress Xiaolie in the ninth chamber of the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Remove Renzong and enshrine Empress Xiaolie in the Grand Temple's ninth chamber.

sentences.zh: 」因上祧祔儀注。

translations.literal: " They thereupon submitted the ceremonial regulations for removal and enshrinement.
translations.idiomatic: " They then submitted the prescribed rites for removal and enshrinement.

sentences.zh: 已而請忌日祭，帝猶銜前議，報曰：「孝烈繼后，所奉者又入繼之君，忌不祭亦可。

translations.literal: Soon they requested sacrifices on the death anniversary; the emperor still harbored the earlier debate and replied: "Xiaolie was a successor empress; the ruler she served was also an adopted succession; not offering the death-anniversary sacrifice is also acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: They soon asked for death-anniversary sacrifices; the emperor, still smarting from the earlier dispute, replied: "Xiaolie was a successor empress, and the ruler she served was an adopted heir—skipping the anniversary sacrifice is acceptable.

sentences.zh: 」階等請益力，帝曰：「非天子不議禮。

translations.literal: " Xu and the others pleaded all the more forcefully; the emperor said: "Only the Son of Heaven may debate rites.
translations.idiomatic: " Xu pressed harder still; the emperor said: "Only the Son of Heaven may debate rites.

sentences.zh: 后當祔廟，居朕室次，禮官顧謂今日未宜，徒飾說以惑眾聽。

translations.literal: The empress should be enshrined in the temple and occupy the chamber next to mine—yet the rites officials say today is not appropriate, merely dressing up excuses to mislead public opinion.
translations.idiomatic: The empress belongs in the temple beside my chamber, yet the rites officials claim the time is wrong—nothing but polished excuses to mislead the court.

sentences.zh: 」因諭嚴嵩等曰：「禮官從朕言，勉強耳。

translations.literal: " He thereupon instructed Yan Song and others: "The rites officials follow my words only with reluctance.
translations.idiomatic: " He then told Yan Song and the others: "The rites officials go along with me only grudgingly.

sentences.zh: 即不忍祧仁宗，且置后主別廟，將來由臣下議處。

translations.literal: If unwilling to remove Renzong, then for now set up a separate temple for the deceased empress; let subjects deliberate in the future.
translations.idiomatic: If you cannot bear to remove Renzong, set up a separate shrine for the late empress for now and leave the final arrangement to your ministers later.

sentences.zh: 忌日令奠一卮酒，不至傷情。

translations.literal: On the death anniversary, order an offering of one cup of wine—not enough to wound the feelings.
translations.idiomatic: On her death anniversary, offer a single cup of wine—that will not wound anyone's feelings.

sentences.zh: 」於是禮臣不敢復言，第請如敕行。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the rites officials dared speak no further, merely requesting to act as the edict commanded.
translations.idiomatic: " The rites officials dared say no more and asked only to carry out the edict.

sentences.zh: 乃許之。

translations.literal: He then granted it.
translations.idiomatic: He granted their request.

sentences.zh: 後二年，楊思忠為賀表觸忌，予杖削籍。

translations.literal: Two years later, Yang Sizhong, in a congratulatory memorial, touched on a taboo subject; he was beaten with the stick and struck from the registers.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later Yang Sizhong, in a congratulatory memorial, hit a taboo and was beaten with the stick and struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，與孝潔皇后同日上尊諡曰「孝烈端順敏惠恭誠祗天衛聖皇后」，移主弘孝殿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longqing, on the same day as Empress Xiaojie, the elevated honorific title "Empress Xiaolie Duanshun Minhui Gongcheng Zhitian Weisheng" was granted, and the spirit tablet was moved to Hongxiao Hall.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Longqing, on the same day as Empress Xiaojie, she received the elevated posthumous title "Empress Xiaolie Duanshun Minhui Gongcheng Zhitian Weisheng," and her tablet was moved to Hongxiao Hall.

sentences.zh: 孝恪杜太后，穆宗生母也，大興人。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Du the Xiaoke was the birth mother of Emperor Muzong, a native of Daxing.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Du, known posthumously as Xiaoke and birth mother of Emperor Muzong, came from Daxing.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十年封康嬪。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Jiajing she was enfeoffed as Lady Kang.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of the Jiajing reign she was made Lady Kang.

sentences.zh: 十五年進封妃。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year she was advanced to the rank of consort.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year she was promoted to consort.

sentences.zh: 三十三年正月薨。

translations.literal: In the first month of the thirty-third year she died.
translations.idiomatic: She died in the first month of the thirty-third year.

sentences.zh: 是時，穆宗以裕王居邸，禮部尚書歐陽德奏喪儀，請輟朝五日，裕王主喪事，遵高皇帝《孝慈錄》，斬衰三年。

translations.literal: At that time Muzong as Prince of Yu resided at his princely mansion; Minister of Rites Ouyang De submitted the mourning rites, requesting five days' suspension of court, with the Prince of Yu presiding over the funeral, following the Founding Emperor's Record of Filial Affection in wearing hemp of the severest grade for three years.
translations.idiomatic: Muzong was then Prince of Yu living in his mansion; Minister of Rites Ouyang De laid out the mourning rites, asking for five days' court suspension, with the prince presiding and wearing the severest three-year hemp mourning prescribed in the Founding Emperor's Record of Filial Affection.

sentences.zh: 帝謂當避君父之尊。

translations.literal: The emperor said one must defer to the honor of the ruler and father.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said one must respect the superior status of the ruler and father.

sentences.zh: 大學士嚴嵩言：「高帝命周王橚為孫貴妃服慈母服，斬衰三年。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Yan Song said: "The Founding Emperor ordered Prince Zhou Xu to wear the nurturer-mother mourning for Grand Consort Sun, hemp of the severest grade for three years.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Yan Song said: "The Founding Emperor ordered Prince Zhou Xu to wear three years of severest hemp mourning for Grand Consort Sun as for a nurturing mother.

sentences.zh: 是年，《孝慈錄》成，遂為定制，自後久無是事。

translations.literal: That year the Record of Filial Affection was completed and became fixed precedent; afterward such matters had long been absent.
translations.idiomatic: That same year the Record of Filial Affection was finished and became standard practice; such cases had been rare ever since.

sentences.zh: 及茲當作則垂訓於后。

translations.literal: Now when such a case arises, it should serve as instruction for posterity.
translations.idiomatic: When one arises now, it should set a precedent for generations to come.

sentences.zh: 」帝命比賢妃鄭氏故事：輟朝二日。

translations.literal: " The emperor ordered following the precedent of Noble Lady Zheng: two days' suspension of court.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor ordered the precedent of Noble Lady Zheng followed: two days' suspension of court.

sentences.zh: 賜諡榮淑，葬金山。

translations.literal: She was granted the posthumous name Rongshu and buried at Jinshan.
translations.idiomatic: She received the posthumous name Rongshu and was buried at Jinshan.

sentences.zh: 穆宗立，上諡曰「孝恪淵純慈懿恭順贊天開聖皇太后」，遷葬永陵，祀主神霄殿。

translations.literal: When Muzong ascended, the posthumous title "Empress Dowager Xiaoke Yuanchun Ciyi Gongshun Zantian Kaisheng" was granted; she was reburied at Yongling and her spirit tablet enshrined in Shenxiao Hall.
translations.idiomatic: When Muzong took the throne she was given the posthumous title "Empress Dowager Xiaoke Yuanchun Ciyi Gongshun Zantian Kaisheng," reburied at Yongling, and her tablet placed in Shenxiao Hall.

sentences.zh: 追封后父林為慶都伯，命其子繼宗嗣​​。

translations.literal: Her father Lin was posthumously enfeoffed as Marquis of Qingdu, and his son Jizong was ordered to inherit.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Lin was posthumously made Marquis of Qingdu, and his son Jizong was appointed to inherit the title.

sentences.zh: 穆宗孝懿皇后李氏，昌平人。

translations.literal: Empress Li the Xiaoyi of Emperor Muzong was a native of Changping.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Li, known posthumously as Xiaoyi and consort of Emperor Muzong, came from Changping.

sentences.zh: 穆宗為裕王，選為妃，生憲懷太子。

translations.literal: When Muzong was Prince of Yu she was chosen as consort and bore the Crown Prince Xianhuai.
translations.idiomatic: While Muzong was Prince of Yu she was chosen as his consort and bore Crown Prince Xianhuai.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三十七年四月薨。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the thirty-seventh year of Jiajing she died.
translations.idiomatic: She died in the fourth month of the thirty-seventh year of Jiajing.

sentences.zh: 帝以部疏稱薨非制，命改稱故，葬金山。

translations.literal: The emperor held that the ministry memorial's use of "died" was not according to regulation and ordered it changed to "deceased"; she was buried at Jinshan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ruled that the ministry's use of "died" was improper and ordered it changed to "deceased"; she was buried at Jinshan.

sentences.zh: 穆宗即位，諡曰「孝懿皇后」，封后父銘德平伯。

translations.literal: When Muzong ascended he granted the posthumous title "Empress Xiaoyi" and enfeoffed her father Ming as Marquis of Deping.
translations.idiomatic: When Muzong took the throne he gave her the posthumous title "Empress Xiaoyi" and made her father Ming Marquis of Deping.

sentences.zh: 神宗即位，上尊諡曰「孝懿貞惠順哲恭仁儷天襄聖莊皇后」，合葬昭陵，祔太廟。

translations.literal: When Shenzong ascended, the elevated honorific title "Empress Xiaoyi Zhenhui Shunzhe Gongren Litian Xiangsheng Zhuang" was granted; she was buried with the emperor at Zhaoling and enshrined in the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenzong ascended she received the elevated posthumous title "Empress Xiaoyi Zhenhui Shunzhe Gongren Litian Xiangsheng Zhuang," was buried with him at Zhaoling, and enshrined in the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 孝定李太后，神宗生母也，漷縣人。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Li the Xiaoding was the birth mother of Emperor Shenzong, a native of Huoxian.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Li, known posthumously as Xiaoding and birth mother of Emperor Shenzong, came from Huoxian.

sentences.zh: 侍穆宗於裕邸。

translations.literal: She attended Muzong at the Prince of Yu's mansion.
translations.idiomatic: She served Muzong while he was Prince of Yu.

sentences.zh: 隆慶元年三月封貴妃。

translations.literal: In the third month of the first year of Longqing she was enfeoffed as Imperial Noble Consort.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the first year of Longqing she was made Imperial Noble Consort.

sentences.zh: 生神宗。

translations.literal: She bore Shenzong.
translations.idiomatic: She bore Shenzong.

sentences.zh: 即位，上尊號曰慈聖皇太后。

translations.literal: Upon his accession the elevated honorific title Cisheng Empress Dowager was granted.
translations.idiomatic: When he ascended the throne she was honored as Empress Dowager Cisheng.

sentences.zh: 舊制：天子立，尊皇后為皇太后，若有生母稱太后者，則加徽號以別之。

translations.literal: Old precedent: when the Son of Heaven ascended, the empress was honored as Empress Dowager; if the birth mother also bore the title Empress Dowager, an honorific epithet was added to distinguish them.
translations.idiomatic: By old custom, when a new emperor took the throne the empress became Empress Dowager; if the birth mother also held that title, an honorific epithet distinguished the two.

sentences.zh: 是時，太監馮保欲媚貴妃，因以並尊風大學士張居正下廷臣議，尊皇后曰「仁聖皇太后」，貴妃曰「慈聖皇太后」，始無別矣。

translations.literal: At that time the eunuch Feng Bao, wishing to please the Noble Consort, carried a trend of joint equal honor through Grand Secretary Zhang Juzheng to the court officials for deliberation: the empress was honored as "Rensheng Empress Dowager" and the Noble Consort as "Cisheng Empress Dowager"—there was no distinction from the start.
translations.idiomatic: Then the eunuch Feng Bao, currying favor with the Noble Consort, pushed through Zhang Juzheng a joint elevation: the empress was styled "Empress Dowager Rensheng" and the Noble Consort "Empress Dowager Cisheng"—from the outset they were equals.

sentences.zh: 仁聖居慈慶宮，慈聖居慈寧宮。

translations.literal: Rensheng resided in Ciqing Palace; Cisheng in Cining Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Rensheng lived in Ciqing Palace; Cisheng in Cining Palace.

sentences.zh: 居正請太后視帝起居，乃徙居乾清宮。

translations.literal: Juzheng requested that the Empress Dowager oversee the emperor's daily conduct, and she then moved to the Palace of Heavenly Purity.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng asked that she oversee the emperor's daily life, and she moved to the Palace of Heavenly Purity.

sentences.zh: 太后教帝頗嚴。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager taught the emperor quite strictly.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager raised the emperor with considerable strictness.

sentences.zh: 帝或不讀書，即召使長跪。

translations.literal: If the emperor did not study, she would summon him to kneel for long periods.
translations.idiomatic: If he neglected his books, she had him kneel for long stretches.

sentences.zh: 每御講筵入，嘗令效講臣進講於前。

translations.literal: Whenever he entered the lecture hall, she would often have him imitate the lecturing officials and deliver a lecture before her.
translations.idiomatic: Before each lecture session she often made him play the lecturer and recite a lesson in front of her.

sentences.zh: 遇朝期，五更至帝寢所，呼曰「帝起」，敕左右掖帝坐，取水為盥面，挈之登輦以出。

translations.literal: On days of court audience, at the fifth watch she would come to the emperor's bedchamber, call "The emperor rises," order attendants to support him to sit, fetch water for washing his face, and lead him to mount the palanquin and go out.
translations.idiomatic: On court days, at the fifth watch she went to his bedchamber, called "Rise, Your Majesty," had attendants help him sit up, brought water to wash his face, and led him to the palanquin.

sentences.zh: 帝事太后惟謹，而諸內臣奉太后旨者，往往挾持太過。

translations.literal: The emperor served the Empress Dowager with utmost deference, yet the inner officials who carried out her orders often overstepped in wielding her authority.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor treated her with scrupulous deference, but inner officials acting on her orders often abused her authority.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗在西城曲宴被酒，令內侍歌新聲，辭不能，取劍擊之。

translations.literal: The emperor once held a private banquet in the western city while drunk, ordered an inner attendant to sing a new tune; when he declined, the emperor took a sword and struck him.
translations.idiomatic: Once, drunk at a private banquet in the western city, he ordered an attendant to sing a new song; when the man refused, the emperor struck him with a sword.

sentences.zh: 左右勸解，乃戲割其發。

translations.literal: Attendants urged him to stop; he then playfully cut off the man's hair.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants pulled him off; he then jokingly cut the man's hair.

sentences.zh: 翼日，太后聞，傳語居正具疏切諫，令為帝草罪己御札。

translations.literal: The next day, when the Empress Dowager heard, she sent word to Juzheng to prepare a memorial of stern remonstrance and to draft for the emperor an imperial letter of self-reproach.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, hearing of it, she sent word to Juzheng to submit a sharp remonstrance and draft a self-reproach edict for the emperor.

sentences.zh: 又召帝長跪，數其過。

translations.literal: She also summoned the emperor to kneel long and enumerated his faults.
translations.idiomatic: She also had the emperor kneel and listed his offenses one by one.

sentences.zh: 帝涕泣請改乃已。

translations.literal: The emperor wept and begged to reform before she desisted.
translations.idiomatic: He wept and promised to mend his ways before she relented.

sentences.zh: 六年，帝大婚，太后將返慈寧宮，敕居正曰：「吾不能視皇帝朝夕，先生親受先帝付託，其朝夕納誨，終先帝憑幾之誼。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, when the emperor's grand wedding was held, the Empress Dowager was to return to Cining Palace and charged Juzheng: "I cannot watch over the emperor morning and evening; you personally received the late emperor's trust—receive his admonitions morning and evening and fulfill the late emperor's charge at his deathbed.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, as the emperor's grand wedding approached and she was to return to Cining Palace, she told Juzheng: "I can no longer watch over the emperor day and night; you personally received the late emperor's trust—guide him daily and honor the charge the late emperor gave you at his deathbed.

sentences.zh: 」三月加尊號曰「宣文」。

translations.literal: " In the third month the honorific "Xuanwen" was added.
translations.idiomatic: " In the third month "Xuanwen" was added to her titles.

sentences.zh: 十年加「明肅」。

translations.literal: In the tenth year "Mingsu" was added.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year "Mingsu" was added.

sentences.zh: 十二年同仁聖太后謁山陵。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year she joined Empress Dowager Rensheng in visiting the imperial tombs.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year she joined Empress Dowager Rensheng on a visit to the imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 二十九年加貞壽端獻。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year Zhenshou Duandian was added.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year Zhenshou Duandian was added.

sentences.zh: 三十四年加恭熹。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year Gongxi was added.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fourth year Gongxi was added.

sentences.zh: 四十二年二月崩，上尊諡曰「孝定貞純欽仁端肅弼天祚聖皇太后」，合葬昭陵，別祀崇先殿。

translations.literal: In the second month of the forty-second year she died; the elevated honorific posthumous title "Empress Dowager Xiaoding Zhenchun Qinren Duansu Bitian Zuosheng" was granted; she was buried with the emperor at Zhaoling and separately enshrined at Chongxian Hall.
translations.idiomatic: She died in the second month of the forty-second year and received the elevated posthumous title "Empress Dowager Xiaoding Zhenchun Qinren Duansu Bitian Zuosheng"; she was buried with the emperor at Zhaoling and separately enshrined at Chongxian Hall.

sentences.zh: 后性嚴明。

translations.literal: The empress dowager's nature was stern and clear.
translations.idiomatic: She was stern and clear-minded by nature.

sentences.zh: 萬曆初政，委任張居正，綜核名實，幾於富強，后之力居多。

translations.literal: In the early Wanli reign she entrusted Zhang Juzheng; he coordinated names with realities and brought the state nearly to wealth and strength—the empress dowager's contribution was greatest.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Wanli years she backed Zhang Juzheng; he matched names to realities and nearly restored prosperity and strength—and her role was the largest.

sentences.zh: 光宗之未冊立也，給事中姜應麟等疏請被謫，太后聞之弗善。

translations.literal: Before Guangzong was designated heir, supervising secretaries Jiang Yinglin and others memorialized requesting it and were demoted; when the Empress Dowager heard she was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Before Guangzong was named heir, supervising secretaries Jiang Yinglin and others petitioned for his appointment and were demoted; the Empress Dowager was displeased when she heard.

sentences.zh: 一日，帝入侍，太后問故。

translations.literal: One day, when the emperor came to attend her, the Empress Dowager asked the reason.
translations.idiomatic: One day, as the emperor attended her, she asked why.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「彼都人子也。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "He is a capital palace woman's son.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "He is the son of a palace woman.

sentences.zh: 」太后大怒曰：「爾亦都人子！

translations.literal: " The Empress Dowager said in great anger: "You too are a capital palace woman's son!
translations.idiomatic: " The Empress Dowager flared up: "You are a palace woman's son too!

sentences.zh: 」帝惶恐，伏地不敢起。

translations.literal: " The emperor was terrified and prostrated himself, not daring to rise.
translations.idiomatic: " Terrified, he prostrated himself and did not dare rise.

sentences.zh: 蓋內廷呼宮人曰「都人」，太后亦由宮人進，故云。

translations.literal: For within the palace, palace women were called "capital people"; the Empress Dowager had also entered by the palace-woman route, hence the remark.
translations.idiomatic: Within the palace, palace women were called "capital people"; the Empress Dowager had risen from that rank herself, which is why she said it.

sentences.zh: 光宗由是得立。

translations.literal: Guangzong was thereby established as heir.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzong was thereby made heir.

sentences.zh: 群臣請福王之籓，行有日矣，鄭貴妃欲遲之明年，以祝太后誕為解。

translations.literal: When the officials requested that the Prince of Fu go to his fief—the day of departure was set—Noble Consort Zheng wished to delay until the next year, citing celebration of the Empress Dowager's birthday as excuse.
translations.idiomatic: When officials asked that the Prince of Fu leave for his fief—with a date already set—Noble Consort Zheng wanted to delay until the next year, citing the Empress Dowager's birthday.

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「吾潞王亦可來上壽乎！

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager said: "Could my Prince of Lu also come to offer birthday felicitations!
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager said: "Should my Prince of Lu also come to offer birthday wishes!

sentences.zh: 」貴妃乃不敢留福王。

translations.literal: " The Noble Consort then dared not keep the Prince of Fu.
translations.idiomatic: " The Noble Consort then dared not keep the Prince of Fu any longer.

sentences.zh: 御史曹學程以建言論死。

translations.literal: Censor Cao Xuecheng was sentenced to death for his remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Cao Xuecheng was sentenced to death for speaking out.

sentences.zh: 太后憐其母老，言於帝，釋之。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager, pitying his aged mother, spoke to the emperor and he was released.
translations.idiomatic: Pitying his elderly mother, the Empress Dowager appealed to the emperor and he was pardoned.

sentences.zh: 后父​​偉封武清伯。

translations.literal: Her father Wei was enfeoffed as Marquis of Wuqing.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Wei was made Marquis of Wuqing.

sentences.zh: 家人嘗有過，命中使出數之，而抵其家人於法。

translations.literal: When her household once committed offenses, she ordered eunuchs to enumerate them, yet had her household members answer to the law.
translations.idiomatic: When members of her household once broke the law, she had eunuchs rebuke them but still handed the offenders over for punishment.

sentences.zh: 顧好佛，京師內外多置梵剎，動費鉅萬，帝亦助施無算。

translations.literal: Yet she favored Buddhism; inside and outside the capital many Buddhist temples were established, often costing tens of thousands; the emperor also contributed immeasurable sums.
translations.idiomatic: Yet she was devoted to Buddhism; temples sprang up across the capital at a cost of tens of thousands each, and the emperor gave without counting.

sentences.zh: 居正在日，嘗以為言，未能用也。

translations.literal: While Juzheng was alive he once spoke of this but could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: While Juzheng lived he raised the matter once but could not stop it.

sentences.zh: 神宗孝端皇后王氏，余姚人，生京師。

translations.literal: Empress Wang the Xiaoduan of Emperor Shenzong was a native of Yuyao and born in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wang, known posthumously as Xiaoduan and consort of Emperor Shenzong, came from Yuyao and was born in the capital.

sentences.zh: 萬曆六年冊立為皇后。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Wanli she was invested as empress.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Wanli she was invested as empress.

sentences.zh: 性端謹，事孝定太后得其歡心。

translations.literal: Her nature was dignified and careful; in serving Empress Dowager Xiaoding she won her favor.
translations.idiomatic: Dignified and careful by nature, she won Empress Dowager Xiaoding's affection.

sentences.zh: 光宗在東宮，危疑者數矣，調護備至。

translations.literal: When Guangzong was in the Eastern Palace, danger and doubt arose many times; she protected and cared for him with utmost thoroughness.
translations.idiomatic: While Guangzong was crown prince, he faced repeated crises; she shielded and cared for him throughout.

sentences.zh: 鄭貴妃顓寵，后不較也。

translations.literal: Noble Consort Zheng monopolized favor; the empress did not contend.
translations.idiomatic: Noble Consort Zheng held the emperor's exclusive favor; the empress did not compete.

sentences.zh: 正位中宮者四十二年，以慈孝稱。

translations.literal: She held the central palace for forty-two years and was known for kindness and filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: She held the central palace for forty-two years and was known for her kindness and filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 四十八年四月崩，諡孝端。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the forty-eighth year she died; posthumous name Xiaoduan.
translations.idiomatic: She died in the fourth month of the forty-eighth year and received the posthumous name Xiaoduan.

sentences.zh: 光宗即位，上尊諡曰「孝端貞恪莊惠仁明媲天毓聖顯皇后」。

translations.literal: When Guangzong ascended, the elevated honorific title "Empress Xiaoduan Zhenke Zhuanghui Renming Pitian Yusheng Xian" was granted.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangzong took the throne she received the elevated posthumous title "Empress Xiaoduan Zhenke Zhuanghui Renming Pitian Yusheng Xian."

sentences.zh: 會帝崩，熹宗立，始上冊寶，合葬定陵，主祔廟。

translations.literal: When the emperor soon died and Xizong ascended, the empress regalia was finally conferred; she was buried with him at Dingling and her spirit tablet enshrined in the temple.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor soon died; when Xizong ascended, her empress regalia was at last conferred, she was buried with him at Dingling, and her tablet was enshrined in the temple.

sentences.zh: 與后同日冊封者有昭妃劉氏。

translations.literal: Enfeoffed on the same day as the empress was Consort Liu the Zhaohui.
translations.idiomatic: Invested on the same day as the empress was Consort Liu, styled Zhaohui.

sentences.zh: 天啟、崇禎時，嘗居慈寧宮，掌太后璽。

translations.literal: During the Tianqi and Chongzhen reigns she often resided in Cining Palace and held the Empress Dowager's seal.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Tianqi and Chongzhen emperors she often lived in Cining Palace and held the empress dowager's seal.

sentences.zh: 性謹厚，撫愛諸王。

translations.literal: Her nature was careful and generous; she nurtured and loved the princes.
translations.idiomatic: Careful and warm by nature, she nurtured the princes with affection.

sentences.zh: 莊烈帝禮事之如大母。

translations.literal: The Chonglie Emperor treated her with ceremony as a great dowager.
translations.idiomatic: The Chongzhen Emperor honored her as a great imperial dowager.

sentences.zh: 嘗以歲朝朝見，帝就便坐，俄假寐。

translations.literal: Once at the New Year's audience she came to pay court; the emperor sat at ease and soon dozed off.
translations.idiomatic: Once at the New Year audience she came to court; the emperor sat informally and soon fell asleep.

sentences.zh: 太后戒勿驚，命尚衣謹護之。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager warned them not to startle him and ordered the Director of Imperial Wardrobe to protect him carefully.
translations.idiomatic: She warned attendants not to wake him abruptly and told the Director of Imperial Wardrobe to guard him carefully.

sentences.zh: 頃之，帝覺，攝衣冠起謝曰：「神祖時海內少事；

translations.literal: Presently the emperor awoke, straightened his robes and rose to apologize: "In the time of the Divine Ancestor there were few affairs under Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: He soon woke, straightened his robes, and apologized: "In the Divine Ancestor's day the realm had few troubles;

sentences.zh: 今苦多難，兩夜省文書，未嘗交睫，在太妃前，困不自持如此。

translations.literal: now troubles are many and bitter; for two nights I have reviewed documents without closing my eyes—in the presence of the Grand Consort I was so weary I could not hold myself together.
translations.idiomatic: now hardship is everywhere; for two nights I have gone over documents without sleep—in your presence I was too exhausted to keep myself upright.

sentences.zh: 」太妃為之泣下。

translations.literal: " The Grand Consort wept at this.
translations.idiomatic: " The Grand Consort wept at his words.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十五年薨，年八十有六。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Chongzhen she died, aged eighty-six.
translations.idiomatic: She died in the fifteenth year of Chongzhen, at the age of eighty-six.

sentences.zh: 孝靖王太后，光宗生母也。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Wang the Xiaojing, birth mother of Emperor Guangzong.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Wang (Xiaojing), birth mother of Emperor Guangzong.

sentences.zh: 初為慈寧宮宮人。

translations.literal: At first she was a palace woman of the Cining Palace.
translations.idiomatic: She began as a maid in the Cining Palace.

sentences.zh: 年長矣，帝過慈寧，私幸之，有身。

translations.literal: She was already advanced in years; the emperor passed through Cining, privately favored her, and she became pregnant.
translations.idiomatic: She was no longer young when the emperor passed through Cining, took her secretly to bed, and she conceived.

sentences.zh: 故事：宮中承寵，必有賞賚，文書房內侍記年月及所賜以為驗。

translations.literal: Precedent held that when a woman in the palace received the emperor's favor, rewards must be given, and eunuchs of the Imperial Secretariat would record the year, month, and gifts received as proof.
translations.idiomatic: By established custom, when a palace woman received the emperor's favor, gifts were always bestowed, and eunuchs of the Imperial Secretariat recorded the date and what was given as verification.

sentences.zh: 時帝諱之，故左右無言者。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor kept it secret, so those around him said nothing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to conceal the affair, so those at his side kept silent.

sentences.zh: 一日，侍慈聖宴，語及之。

translations.literal: One day, while attending a banquet of Empress Dowager Cisheng, she spoke of the matter.
translations.idiomatic: One day at a banquet hosted by Empress Dowager Cisheng, the topic was raised.

sentences.zh: 帝不應。

translations.literal: The emperor did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gave no answer.

sentences.zh: 慈聖命取內起居注示帝，且好語曰：「吾老矣，猶未有孫。

translations.literal: Cisheng ordered the Inner Daily Records brought to show the emperor, and said kindly: "I am old, yet still have no grandson.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Cisheng had the Inner Daily Records fetched to show the emperor and spoke gently: "I am old, and still have no grandson.

sentences.zh: 果男者，宗社福也。

translations.literal: If it is indeed a boy, it will be a blessing to the ancestral temple and the state.
translations.idiomatic: If the child is a boy, that will be a blessing to the dynasty and the realm.

sentences.zh: 母以子貴，寧分差等耶？

translations.literal: When a mother is ennobled through her son, can one still insist on distinctions of rank?
translations.idiomatic: A mother rises in station through her son—why cling to differences of rank?

sentences.zh: 」十年四月封恭妃。

translations.literal: " In the fourth month of the tenth year she was enfeoffed as Consort Gong.
translations.idiomatic: " In the fourth month of the tenth year she was created Consort Gong.

sentences.zh: 八月，光宗生，是為皇長子。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Guangzong was born; he was the eldest imperial son.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Guangzong was born—the future crown prince and eldest son.

sentences.zh: 既而鄭貴妃生皇三子，進封皇貴妃，而恭妃不進封。

translations.literal: Later Noble Consort Zheng bore the third imperial son and was promoted to Imperial Noble Consort, but Consort Gong received no promotion.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Noble Consort Zheng bore the third imperial son and was raised to Imperial Noble Consort, while Consort Gong was passed over.

sentences.zh: 二十九年冊立皇長子為皇太子，仍不封如故。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year the eldest imperial son was invested as crown prince, yet she still received no enfeoffment as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year the eldest son was formally named crown prince, yet she remained without further rank.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，元孫生，加慈聖徽號，始進封皇貴妃。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year, when a great-grandson was born and Cisheng was given an honorific title, she was at last promoted to Imperial Noble Consort.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fourth year, after the birth of a great-grandson and the granting of an honorific to Empress Dowager Cisheng, she was finally promoted to Imperial Noble Consort.

sentences.zh: 三十九年病革，光宗請旨得往省，宮門猶閉，抉鑰而入。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year, when her illness turned critical, Guangzong obtained permission to visit her; the palace gate was still shut, and he forced the lock to enter.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-ninth year, as she lay dying, Guangzong secured permission to see her, but found the gate still barred and broke the lock to enter.

sentences.zh: 妃目眚，手光宗衣而泣曰：「兒長大如此，我死何恨！

translations.literal: The consort's eyes were dim; she grasped Guangzong's robe and wept, saying: "My son has grown to such stature—what regret can I have in dying!
translations.idiomatic: Her sight was failing; she seized Guangzong's sleeve and wept: "My son has grown so tall—what regret can I have in dying!

sentences.zh: 」遂薨。

translations.literal: " Thereupon she passed away.
translations.idiomatic: " With that she died.

sentences.zh: 大學士葉向高言：「皇太子母妃薨，禮宜從厚。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Ye Xianggao said: "The crown prince's mother the consort has died; ritual propriety calls for generous treatment.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Ye Xianggao argued: "The crown prince's mother has died—the rites ought to be generous.

sentences.zh: 」不報。

translations.literal: " There was no reply.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor did not respond.

sentences.zh: 復請，乃得允。

translations.literal: He petitioned again and only then obtained approval.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized again, and only then was approval granted.

sentences.zh: 諡溫肅端靖純懿皇貴妃，葬天壽山。

translations.literal: She was given the posthumous title Imperial Noble Consort Wensu Duanjing Chunyi and buried at Tianshou Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: She was posthumously titled Imperial Noble Consort Wensu Duanjing Chunyi and interred at Tianshou Mountain.

sentences.zh: 光宗即位，下詔曰：「朕嗣承基緒，撫臨萬方，溯厥慶源，則我生母溫肅端靖純懿皇貴妃恩莫大焉。

translations.literal: When Guangzong ascended the throne, he issued an edict: "I have inherited the foundation and govern the myriad regions; tracing the source of my good fortune, there is none to whom I owe more than my birth mother, Imperial Noble Consort Wensu Duanjing Chunyi.
translations.idiomatic: At Guangzong's accession he proclaimed: "Having taken up the foundational inheritance and coming to rule all under Heaven, I trace the wellspring of my fortune—and no debt is greater than that owed my birth mother, Imperial Noble Consort Wensu Duanjing Chunyi.

sentences.zh: 朕昔在青宮，莫親溫凊，今居禁闥，徒痛桮棬，欲伸罔極之深悰，惟有肇稱乎殷禮。

translations.literal: Formerly in the Eastern Palace I could not attend to her warmth and coolness; now dwelling within the forbidden precincts I can only grieve over the cup and bowl; to express boundless filial feeling, I must begin by invoking the rituals of the Yin dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: In the Eastern Palace I could not care for her comfort; now within the inner palace I can only mourn over daily offerings. To express the depth of filial devotion I owe her, I must begin with the ancient rites of honoring a royal mother.

sentences.zh: 其準皇祖穆宗皇帝尊生母榮淑康妃故事，禮部詳議以聞。

translations.literal: Let the Ministry of Rites follow the precedent of our imperial ancestor Emperor Muzong's honoring of his birth mother, Consort Rongshu Kang, deliberate in detail, and report.
translations.idiomatic: Let the Ministry of Rites follow the precedent set when our imperial ancestor Emperor Muzong honored his birth mother, Consort Rongshu Kang, deliberate fully, and report back.

sentences.zh: 」會崩，熹宗即位，上尊諡曰「孝靖溫懿敬讓貞慈參天胤聖皇太后」，遷葬定陵，祀奉慈殿。

translations.literal: " Before this could be carried out he died; when Xizong took the throne, she was given the elevated posthumous title "Empress Dowager Xiaojing Wenyi Jingrang Zhenci Cantian Yin Sheng," reinterred at Dingling, and enshrined in the Fengci Hall.
translations.idiomatic: " Before this could be enacted Guangzong died; when Xizong ascended the throne, she received the elevated posthumous title Empress Dowager Xiaojing Wenyi Jingrang Zhenci Cantian Yin Sheng, was reinterred at Dingling, and given offerings in the Fengci Hall.

sentences.zh: 后父​​天瑞，封永寧伯。

translations.literal: The empress dowager's father Tianrui was enfeoffed as Baron of Yongning.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Tianrui was created Baron of Yongning.

sentences.zh: 恭恪貴妃鄭氏，大興人。

translations.literal: Respectful and Earnest Noble Consort Zheng was a native of Daxing.
translations.idiomatic: Noble Consort Zheng (posthumous honorific Gongke), a native of Daxing.

sentences.zh: 萬曆初入宮，封貴妃，生皇三子，進皇貴妃。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Wanli reign she entered the palace, was made noble consort, bore the third imperial son, and was promoted to imperial noble consort.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Wanli reign she entered the palace, was created noble consort, bore the third imperial son, and was raised to imperial noble consort.

sentences.zh: 帝寵之。

translations.literal: The emperor favored her.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor doted on her.

sentences.zh: 外廷疑妃有立己子謀。

translations.literal: The outer court suspected the consort of plotting to establish her own son as heir.
translations.idiomatic: Officials outside the palace suspected she intended to name her own son as heir.

sentences.zh: 群臣爭言立儲事，章奏累數千百，皆指斥宮闈，攻擊執政。

translations.literal: Ministers vied to speak on the question of establishing the heir; memorials piled up in the thousands, all denouncing the inner palace and attacking those in power.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers repeatedly debated succession; thousands of memorials piled up, denouncing the inner palace and assailing the men in power.

sentences.zh: 帝概置不問。

translations.literal: The emperor for the most part set them aside and made no inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: For the most part the emperor ignored them.

sentences.zh: 由是門戶之禍大起。

translations.literal: From this the calamity of factional strife greatly arose.
translations.idiomatic: From this sprang the great calamity of partisan factional warfare.

sentences.zh: 萬曆二十九年春，皇長子移迎禧宮，十月立為皇太子，而疑者仍未已。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twenty-ninth year of Wanli the eldest imperial son moved to the Xiying Palace; in the tenth month he was invested as crown prince, yet those who doubted still did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Wanli 29 the eldest son moved into the Xiying Palace; in the tenth month he was named crown prince, yet suspicion did not end.

sentences.zh: 先是，侍郎呂坤為按察使時，嘗集《閨範圖說》。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Vice Minister Lü Kun was provincial surveillance commissioner, he had compiled Illustrations and Explanations of Women's Virtues in the Inner Quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while serving as provincial surveillance commissioner, Vice Minister Lü Kun had compiled Illustrations and Explanations of Women's Virtues in the Inner Quarters.

sentences.zh: 太監陳矩見之，持以進帝。

translations.literal: Eunuch Chen Ju saw it and presented it to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuch Chen Ju obtained a copy and presented it to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝賜妃，妃重刻之，坤無與也。

translations.literal: The emperor gave it to the consort; she had it reprinted, and Kun had no part in it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gave it to the consort, who had it reprinted—Kun had nothing to do with that.

sentences.zh: 二十六年秋，或撰《閨範圖說跋》，名曰《憂危竑議》，匿其名，盛傳京師，謂《坤書》首載漢明德馬后由宮人進位中宮，意以指妃，而妃之刊刻，實藉此為立己子之據。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the twenty-sixth year someone wrote a postface to Illustrations and Explanations of Women's Virtues in the Inner Quarters titled Discussion of Youwei Jiyong, concealing his name; it spread widely in the capital, saying that Kun's book opened with Empress Ma the Mingde of Han, who rose from palace woman to middle palace—the intent being to point at the consort, and that her reprinting in fact relied on this as grounds to establish her own son.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the twenty-sixth year someone anonymously composed a postface to Illustrations and Explanations of Women's Virtues in the Inner Quarters, titled Discussion of Youwei Jiyong; it circulated widely in the capital, arguing that Lü Kun's book opened with Han Empress Ma the Mingde, who rose from palace maid to empress—a pointed allusion to the consort—and that her reprinting was meant to lend credence to naming her own son as heir.

sentences.zh: 其文托「硃東吉」為問答。

translations.literal: The text used "Zhu Dongji" as the question-and-answer persona.
translations.idiomatic: The essay posed its argument as a dialogue under the pseudonym "Zhu Dongji."

sentences.zh: 「東吉」者，東朝也。

translations.literal: "Dongji" means the Eastern Court.
translations.idiomatic: "Dongji" stood for the Eastern Court—the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 其名《憂危》，以坤曾有《憂危》一疏，因藉其名以諷，蓋言妖也。

translations.literal: Its title, Youwei, drew on Kun's earlier memorial titled Youwei; it borrowed his name as satire—it was essentially a piece of sorcery talk.
translations.idiomatic: The title Youwei alluded to a memorial on peril that Lü Kun had once submitted; by borrowing his name it offered satire—in essence, sedition posing as prophecy.

sentences.zh: 妃兄國泰、侄承恩以給事中戴士衡嘗糾坤，全椒知縣樊玉衡並糾貴妃，疑出自二人手。

translations.literal: The consort's brother Guotai and nephew Chengen, noting that Censor Dai Shiheng had once impeached Kun and that Fan Yuheng, magistrate of Quanjiao, had also impeached the noble consort, suspected the work came from the hands of those two men.
translations.idiomatic: The consort's brother Guotai and nephew Chengen, recalling that Censor Dai Shiheng had once impeached Lü Kun and that Fan Yuheng, magistrate of Quanjiao, had also impeached the noble consort, suspected those two were the authors.

sentences.zh: 帝重謫二人，而置妖言不問。

translations.literal: The emperor heavily demoted the two men but left the sedition untried.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heavily punished the two men but ignored the seditious text itself.

sentences.zh: 逾五年，《續憂危竑議》復出。

translations.literal: More than five years later, A Continuation of the Youwei Jiyong Discussion appeared again.
translations.idiomatic: More than five years later A Continuation of the Youwei Jiyong Discussion circulated again.

sentences.zh: 是時太子已立，大學士硃賡得是書以聞。
