translations.literal: By then the crown prince had already been invested; Grand Secretary Zhu Geng obtained the book and reported it.
translations.idiomatic: By then the crown prince was already named; Grand Secretary Zhu Geng obtained the tract and reported it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 書托「鄭福成」為問答。

translations.literal: The book used "Zheng Fucheng" as the question-and-answer persona.
translations.idiomatic: The tract cast its argument as a dialogue under the name "Zheng Fucheng."

sentences.zh: 「鄭福成」者，謂鄭之福王當成也。

translations.literal: "Zheng Fucheng" meant that the Prince of Fu of the Zheng clan ought to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: "Zheng Fucheng" meant that the Zheng family's Prince of Fu was destined to succeed.

sentences.zh: 大略言：「帝於東宮不得已而立，他日必易。

translations.literal: In broad terms it said: "The emperor established the Eastern Palace heir only because he had no choice; one day he will certainly be replaced.
translations.idiomatic: It declared in essence: "The emperor named the Eastern Palace heir only under compulsion; one day the heir will surely be changed.

sentences.zh: 其特用硃賡內閣者，實寓更易之義。

translations.literal: That it specifically used Zhu Geng of the Grand Secretariat was in fact a hidden meaning of replacement.
translations.idiomatic: Its especial use of Grand Secretary Zhu Geng was a coded hint at replacing the heir.

sentences.zh: 」詞尤詭妄，時皆謂之妖書。

translations.literal: " The language was especially bizarre and presumptuous; at the time all called it a book of sorcery.
translations.idiomatic: " The language was especially wild and seditious; contemporaries called it a demon book—a text of sedition.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，敕錦衣衛搜捕甚急。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly enraged and ordered the Embroidered Uniform Guard to search and seize with great urgency.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and ordered the Embroidered Uniform Guard to hunt down the authors with all speed.

sentences.zh: 久之，乃得皦生光者，坐極刑，語詳郭正域、沈鯉傳。

translations.literal: After a long time a man named Jiao Shengguang was found; he suffered capital punishment; details are given in the biographies of Guo Zhengyu and Shen Li.
translations.idiomatic: After a long search a man named Jiao Shengguang was seized and executed; the full account appears in the biographies of Guo Zhengyu and Shen Li.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，百戶王曰乾又告變，言奸人孔學等為巫蠱，將不利於聖母及太子，語亦及妃。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year, company commander Wang Rigana reported a plot, saying that villains such as Kong Xue practiced witchcraft and meant harm to the Holy Mother and the crown prince; the accusation also implicated the consort.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-first year, company commander Wang Rigana lodged a report of treason, alleging that men such as Kong Xue had used witchcraft against the Holy Mother and crown prince—and implicating the consort as well.

sentences.zh: 賴大學士葉向高勸帝以靜處之，而速福王之籓，以息群言。

translations.literal: Thanks to Grand Secretary Ye Xianggao's counsel that the emperor handle the matter calmly and quickly send the Prince of Fu to his fief, popular talk was stilled.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Ye Xianggao persuaded the emperor to stay calm and speed the Prince of Fu to his fief, quieting public uproar.

sentences.zh: 事乃寢。

translations.literal: The affair then subsided.
translations.idiomatic: The matter died down.

sentences.zh: 其後「梃擊」事起，主事王之寀疏言張差獄情，詞連貴妃宮內侍龐保、劉成等，朝議氵匈氵匈。

translations.literal: Later the "Club Assault" affair arose; Section Director Wang Zhicai memorialized on the circumstances of Zhang Chai's case, linking Palace eunuchs Pang Bao, Liu Cheng, and others of the noble consort's palace; court debate seethed.
translations.idiomatic: Later came the Club Assault affair: Section Director Wang Zhicai memorialized on Zhang Chai's case, implicating eunuchs Pang Bao and Liu Cheng of the noble consort's household; court opinion boiled over.

sentences.zh: 貴妃聞之，對帝泣。

translations.literal: When the noble consort heard of it, she wept before the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: When the noble consort heard of it, she wept before the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「外廷語不易解，若須自求太子。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The talk in the outer court is not easy to dispel; if need be, go yourself to beg the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "This talk outside the palace will not easily die away—you had best go yourself and appeal to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 」貴妃向太子號訴。

translations.literal: " The noble consort went to the crown prince and cried out her plea.
translations.idiomatic: " The noble consort went to the crown prince and poured out her grief.

sentences.zh: 貴妃拜，太子亦拜。

translations.literal: The noble consort bowed, and the crown prince bowed in return.
translations.idiomatic: The noble consort kowtowed, and the crown prince kowtowed in return.

sentences.zh: 帝又於慈寧宮太后几筵前召見群臣，令太子降諭禁株連，於是張差獄乃定。

translations.literal: The emperor again summoned the ministers before the spirit tablet of the Empress Dowager of Cining Palace and had the crown prince issue a directive forbidding implicating others by association; thus Zhang Chai's case was settled.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again assembled the ministers before the memorial tablet of the Cining Empress Dowager and had the crown prince issue orders forbidding guilt by association; Zhang Chai's case was finally closed.

sentences.zh: 神宗崩，遺命封妃皇后。

translations.literal: When Shenzong died, his final command was to enfeoff the consort as empress.
translations.idiomatic: At Shenzong's death his final injunction was to create the consort empress.

sentences.zh: 禮部侍郎孫如游爭之，乃止。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Rites Sun Ruyou disputed it, and the matter was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Rites Sun Ruyou objected, and the plan was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 及光宗崩，有言妃與李選侍同居乾清宮謀垂簾聽政者，久之始息。

translations.literal: When Guangzong died, there were rumors that the consort and Selected Attendant Li lived together in the Qianqing Palace plotting to rule from behind the curtain; only after a long time did the talk die down.
translations.idiomatic: After Guangzong's death, rumors spread that the consort and Selected Attendant Li, dwelling together in the Qianqing Palace, meant to rule from behind a screen; the talk subsided only slowly.

sentences.zh: 崇禎三年七月薨，諡「恭恪惠榮和靖皇貴妃」，葬銀泉山。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the third year of Chongzhen she died; she was given the posthumous title "Respectful, Earnest, Kind, Glorious, Harmonious, and Tranquil Imperial Noble Consort" and buried at Yinquan Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: She died in the seventh month of Chongzhen 3 and was posthumously titled Imperial Noble Consort Gongke Huirong Hejing; she was buried at Yinquan Mountain.

sentences.zh: 光宗孝元皇后郭氏，順天人。

translations.literal: Empress Guo the Xiaoyuan of Emperor Guangzong was a native of Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Guo (posthumous name Xiaoyuan), consort of Emperor Guangzong, came from Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 父維城以女貴，封博平伯，進侯。

translations.literal: Her father Weicheng, ennobled through his daughter's rank, was made Baron of Boping and later promoted to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Weicheng was ennobled when his daughter rose in rank—first as Baron of Boping, then as marquis.

sentences.zh: 卒，兄振明嗣。

translations.literal: When he died, her elder brother Zhenming succeeded to the title.
translations.idiomatic: At his death her elder brother Zhenming inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 后於萬曆二十九年冊為皇太子妃。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year of Wanli she was invested as crown prince's consort.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 29 she was formally installed as crown prince's consort.

sentences.zh: 四十一年十一月薨，諡恭靖。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the forty-first year she died; her posthumous title was Gongjing.
translations.idiomatic: She died in the eleventh month of the forty-first year and received the posthumous name Gongjing.

sentences.zh: 熹宗即位，上尊諡曰「孝元昭懿哲惠莊仁合天弼聖貞皇后」，遷葬慶陵，祔廟。

translations.literal: When Xizong took the throne, she was given the elevated posthumous title "Empress Xiaoyuan Zhaoyi Zhehui Zhuangren Hetian Bisheng Zhen," reinterred at Qingling, and enshrined in the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: At Xizong's accession she received the elevated posthumous title Empress Xiaoyuan Zhaoyi Zhehui Zhuangren Hetian Bisheng Zhen, was reinterred at Qingling, and joined the imperial temple rites.

sentences.zh: 孝和王太后，熹宗生母也，順天人。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Wang the Xiaohe, birth mother of Xizong, was a native of Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Wang (Xiaohe), birth mother of Xizong, came from Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 侍光宗東宮，為選侍。

translations.literal: She attended Guangzong in the Eastern Palace as a selected attendant.
translations.idiomatic: She served in Guangzong's Eastern Palace as a selected attendant.

sentences.zh: 萬曆三十二年進才人。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year of Wanli she was promoted to Lady of Talent.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 32 she was promoted to Lady of Talent.

sentences.zh: 四十七年三月薨。

translations.literal: In the third month of the forty-seventh year she died.
translations.idiomatic: She died in the third month of the forty-seventh year.

sentences.zh: 熹宗即位，上尊諡曰「孝和恭獻溫穆徽慈諧天鞠聖皇太后」，遷葬慶陵，祀奉先殿。

translations.literal: When Xizong took the throne, she was given the elevated posthumous title "Empress Dowager Xiaohe Gongxian Wenmu Huici Xietian Jusheng," reinterred at Qingling, and enshrined in the Fengxian Hall.
translations.idiomatic: At Xizong's accession she received the elevated posthumous title Empress Dowager Xiaohe Gongxian Wenmu Huici Xietian Jusheng, was reinterred at Qingling, and given offerings in the Fengxian Hall.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十一年三月以加上孝純太后尊諡，於御用監得后及孝靖太后玉冊玉寶，始命有司獻於廟。

translations.literal: In the third month of the eleventh year of Chongzhen, when the honorific title of Empress Dowager Xiaochun was being added, jade registers and seals of the empress and Empress Dowager Xiaojing were obtained from the Directorate of Imperial Manufactories, and only then were officials ordered to present them at the temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Chongzhen 11, while adding honorific titles for Empress Dowager Xiaochun, jade registers and seals for the empress and Empress Dowager Xiaojing were recovered from the Directorate of Imperial Manufactories; only then were officials ordered to present them at the temple.

sentences.zh: 忠賢黨王體乾坐怠玩，論死。

translations.literal: Wang Ti'gan of the Wei Zhongxian faction was convicted of negligence and sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ti'gan, a follower of Wei Zhongxian, was found guilty of negligence and condemned to death.

sentences.zh: 蓋距上諡時十有八年矣。

translations.literal: This was indeed eighteen years after the earlier bestowal of honorific titles.
translations.idiomatic: Fully eighteen years had passed since those titles were first granted.

sentences.zh: 孝純劉太后，莊烈帝生母也，海州人，后籍宛平。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Liu the Xiaochun, birth mother of the Chonglie Emperor, was a native of Haizhou; the empress's household registration was at Wanping.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Liu (Xiaochun), birth mother of the Chongzhen Emperor, came from Haizhou; her household was registered at Wanping.

sentences.zh: 初入宮​​為淑女。

translations.literal: When she first entered the palace she was a palace lady.
translations.idiomatic: She first entered the palace as a palace lady.

sentences.zh: 萬曆三十八年十二月生莊烈皇帝。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the thirty-eighth year of Wanli she bore the Chonglie Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of Wanli 38 she bore the future Chongzhen Emperor.

sentences.zh: 已，失光宗意，被譴，薨。

translations.literal: Thereafter she lost Guangzong's favor, was punished, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward she fell from Guangzong's favor, was punished, and died.

sentences.zh: 光宗中悔，恐神宗知之，戒掖庭勿言，葬於西山。

translations.literal: Guangzong later repented, fearing Shenzong would learn of it; he forbade the palace women to speak of it and had her buried on Western Hill.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzong later regretted the matter, fearing Shenzong would discover it; he ordered the inner palace to keep silent and had her buried on Western Hill.

sentences.zh: 及莊烈帝長，封信王，追進賢妃。

translations.literal: When the Chonglie Emperor grew up and was enfeoffed as Prince of Xin, she was posthumously promoted to Consort Xian.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age and was enfeoffed as Prince of Xin, she was posthumously created Consort Xian.

sentences.zh: 時莊烈帝居勗勤宮，問近侍曰：「西山有申懿王墳乎？

translations.literal: At the time the Chonglie Emperor lived in the Xunqin Palace and asked his close attendants: "On Western Hill, is there the tomb of Prince Shenyi?
translations.idiomatic: While living in the Xunqin Palace, the future Chongzhen Emperor asked his attendants: "On Western Hill, is there the tomb of Prince Shenyi?

translations.literal: " They replied: "There is.
translations.idiomatic: " They answered: "There is.

sentences.zh: 」「傍有劉娘娘墳乎？

translations.literal: " "Beside it, is there the tomb of Lady Liu?
translations.idiomatic: " "And beside it, is there the tomb of Lady Liu?

translations.literal: " They replied: "There is.
translations.idiomatic: " They answered: "There is.

sentences.zh: 」每密付金錢往祭。

translations.literal: " Each time he secretly entrusted money for offerings.
translations.idiomatic: " He secretly sent money for offerings again and again.

sentences.zh: 及即位，上尊諡曰「孝純恭懿淑穆莊靜毘天毓聖皇太后」，遷葬慶陵。

translations.literal: When he took the throne, she was given the elevated posthumous title "Empress Dowager Xiaochun Gongyi Shumu Zhuangjing Bitian Yusheng" and reinterred at Qingling.
translations.idiomatic: At his accession she received the elevated posthumous title Empress Dowager Xiaochun Gongyi Shumu Zhuangjing Bitian Yusheng and was reinterred at Qingling.

sentences.zh: 帝五歲失太后，問左右遺像，莫能得。

translations.literal: The emperor lost his mother when he was five; he asked those around him for her portrait, but none could be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: He was five when he lost his mother; he asked those around him for her portrait, but none could be found.

sentences.zh: 傅懿妃者，舊與太后同為淑女，比宮居，自稱習太后，言宮人中狀貌相類者，命后母瀛國太夫人指示畫工，可意得也。

translations.literal: Imperial Concubine Fu Yi had formerly been a palace lady together with the empress dowager; living in the palace together, she claimed to know the empress dowager well and said that among palace women there were those similar in appearance and bearing; the empress dowager's mother, the Grand Lady of Yingguo, was ordered to guide the painters until a likeness satisfactory to the emperor could be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Concubine Fu Yi had once entered the palace as a palace lady alongside the empress dowager; now living in the inner quarters, she claimed intimate knowledge of the empress dowager and said that among palace women there were those of similar appearance; the empress dowager's mother, the Grand Lady of Yingguo, was told to guide the painters until a likeness met with the emperor's approval.

sentences.zh: 圖成，由正陽門具法駕迎入。

translations.literal: When the painting was finished, it was brought in through the Zhengyang Gate with full imperial escort.
translations.idiomatic: When the portrait was finished, it was escorted through the Zhengyang Gate with full imperial ceremony.

sentences.zh: 帝跪迎於午門，懸之宮中，呼老宮婢視之，或曰似，或曰否。

translations.literal: The emperor knelt to receive it at the Meridian Gate, hung it in the palace, and summoned old palace maids to view it; some said it resembled her, some said it did not.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor knelt to receive it at the Meridian Gate, had it hung in the palace, and called old palace women to judge it—some said it resembled her, some said it did not.

sentences.zh: 帝雨泣，六宮皆泣。

translations.literal: The emperor wept as rain falls; all the inner palace wept.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wept openly, and every woman of the inner palace wept with him.

sentences.zh: 故事：生母忌日不設祭，不服青。

translations.literal: Precedent held that on a birth mother's death anniversary no sacrifice was offered and mourning blue was not worn.
translations.idiomatic: By established custom, on a birth mother's death anniversary no rites were performed and mourners did not wear blue.

sentences.zh: 十五年六月，帝以太后故，欲追前代生繼七后，同建一廟，以展孝思。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fifteenth year, for the empress dowager's sake the emperor wished to follow the seven birth and stepmothers of former ages and build one temple jointly, to express filial feeling.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the fifteenth year, moved by devotion to his mother, the emperor proposed honoring the seven birth and stepmothers of prior reigns together in a single temple, to fulfill his filial intent.

sentences.zh: 乃御德政殿，召大學士及禮臣入，問曰：「太廟之制，一帝一后，祧廟亦然，歷朝繼后及生母凡七位皆不得與，即宮中奉先殿亦尚無祭，奈何？

translations.literal: Thereupon he held court at the Dezheng Hall, summoned grand secretaries and ritual officials, and asked: "The system of the Grand Ancestral Temple is one emperor and one empress; the same holds for the collateral temples. Birth and stepmothers of successive reigns—seven in all—may not participate; even in the palace the Fengxian Hall still has no sacrifice for them. What is to be done?
translations.idiomatic: He then held audience at the Dezheng Hall, summoned grand secretaries and ritual officials, and asked: "The Grand Ancestral Temple allows one empress per emperor, and the collateral temples follow the same rule. Seven birth and stepmothers from prior reigns may not share in those rites; even within the palace the Fengxian Hall offers them no sacrifice. What can be done?

sentences.zh: 」禮部侍郎蔣德璟曰：「奉先殿外尚有奉慈殿，所以奉繼后及生母者，雖廢可舉也。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Rites Jiang Dejing said: "Outside the Fengxian Hall there is still the Fengci Hall, which was built to honor stepmothers and birth mothers; though abolished, it can be revived."
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Rites Jiang Dejing replied: "Beyond the Fengxian Hall stands the Fengci Hall, erected to enshrine stepmothers and birth mothers alike. Though it was abandoned, the precedent can be restored."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「奉慈殿外，尚有弘孝、神霄、本恩諸殿。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Outside the Fengci Hall, there are also the Hongxiao, Shenxiao, and Ben'en halls."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Beyond the Fengci Hall lie the Hongxiao, Shenxiao, and Ben'en halls as well."

sentences.zh: 」德璟曰：「內廷規制，臣等未悉。

translations.literal: Dejing said: "As for the regulations of the inner court, we your ministers do not fully know them."
translations.idiomatic: Dejing said: "We ministers are not fully acquainted with the inner court's regulations."

sentences.zh: 孝宗建奉慈殿，嘉靖間廢之，今未知尚有舊基否？

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozong built the Fengci Hall; it was abolished during the Jiajing reign. It is not known now whether the old foundation still remains.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozong had built the Fengci Hall, which was dismantled in the Jiajing reign. Whether any remnant of its original site survives is now unknown.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「奉慈已撤，惟奉先尚可拓也。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The Fengci has been removed; only the Fengxian can still be expanded."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "The Fengci Hall is gone; only the Fengxian Hall can still be enlarged."

sentences.zh: 」於是別置一殿，祀孝純及七后云。

translations.literal: Thereupon a separate hall was set up to enshrine Empress Xiaochun and the seven empresses, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: A separate hall was then established to honor Empress Xiaochun together with the seven empresses.

sentences.zh: 康妃李氏，光​​宗選侍也。

translations.literal: Lady of Imperial Favor Li was a consort-attendant of Emperor Guangzong.
translations.idiomatic: Lady of Imperial Favor Li was a consort-attendant of Emperor Guangzong.

sentences.zh: 時宮中有二李選侍，人稱東、西​​李。

translations.literal: At the time there were two Li consort-attendants in the palace, whom people called Eastern Li and Western Li.
translations.idiomatic: At that time two Li consort-attendants served in the palace, known as Eastern Li and Western Li.

sentences.zh: 康妃者，西李也，最有寵，嘗撫視熹宗及莊烈帝。

translations.literal: The Lady of Imperial Favor was Western Li; she enjoyed the greatest favor and had once cared for Emperor Xizong and Emperor Zhuanglie.
translations.idiomatic: The Lady of Imperial Favor was Western Li, the favorite of the two; she had once helped raise both Emperor Xizong and the future Emperor Zhuanglie.

sentences.zh: 光宗即位，不豫，召大臣入，帝御暖閣，憑幾，命封選侍為皇貴妃。

translations.literal: When Guangzong took the throne, he was unwell; he summoned ministers in. The emperor sat in the warm pavilion, leaning on a desk, and ordered that the consort-attendant be granted the title of Noble Imperial Consort.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangzong ascended the throne he was already ill. Summoning his ministers, he received them in the warm pavilion, leaned on his armrest, and ordered that the consort-attendant be promoted to Noble Imperial Consort.

sentences.zh: 選侍趣熹宗出曰：「欲封后。

translations.literal: The consort-attendant hurried the young Xizong out and said: "I wish to be made empress."
translations.idiomatic: The consort-attendant sent the young Xizong out and said: "I want to be made empress."

sentences.zh: 」帝不應。

translations.literal: The emperor did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor made no answer.

sentences.zh: 禮部侍郎孫如游奏曰：「今兩太后及元妃、才人諡號俱未上，俟四大禮舉行後未晚。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Rites Sun Ruyou memorialized: "At present the posthumous titles of the two empress dowagers, the primary consort, and the ladies of talent have not yet been submitted; it would not be late to wait until after the four major rites have been performed."
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Rites Sun Ruyou submitted a memorial: "The posthumous titles of the two empress dowagers, the primary consort, and the imperial ladies have yet to be announced. There is no harm in waiting until the four state mourning rites are complete."

sentences.zh: 」既而帝崩，選侍尚居乾清宮，外廷恟懼，疑選侍欲聽政。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the emperor died. The consort-attendant still resided in the Palace of Heavenly Purity. The outer court was alarmed and feared, suspecting that the consort-attendant wished to hold court from behind the curtain.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the emperor died, but the consort-attendant remained in the Palace of Heavenly Purity. The court outside grew frightened, suspecting she intended to rule from behind the curtain.

sentences.zh: 大學士劉一燝、吏部尚書周嘉謨、兵科都給事中楊漣、御史左​​光斗等上疏力爭，選侍移居仁壽殿。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Liu Yipao, Minister of Personnel Zhou Jiamo, supervising secretary of the Bureau of War Yang Lian, censor Zuo Guangdou, and others submitted memorials arguing forcefully, and the consort-attendant moved to the Hall of Benevolent Longevity.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Liu Yipao, Minister of Personnel Zhou Jiamo, Yang Lian of the Bureau of War, Censor Zuo Guangdou, and others memorialized in vigorous protest, and the consort-attendant was moved to the Hall of Benevolent Longevity.

sentences.zh: 事詳一燝、漣傳。

translations.literal: The affair is detailed in the biographies of Yipao and Lian.
translations.idiomatic: The full account appears in the biographies of Liu Yipao and Yang Lian.

sentences.zh: 熹宗即位，降敕暴選侍凌毆聖母因致崩逝及妄覬垂簾狀。

translations.literal: When Xizong took the throne, he issued an edict exposing how the consort-attendant had abused and beaten the sacred mother, thereby causing her death, and how she had presumptuously coveted regency from behind the curtain.
translations.idiomatic: When Xizong ascended the throne, he issued an edict denouncing the consort-attendant for abusing the empress dowager until her death and for scheming to rule from behind the curtain.

sentences.zh: 而御史賈繼春進安選侍揭，與周朝瑞爭駁不已。

translations.literal: But Censor Jia Jichun submitted a petition defending the consort-attendant, and he and Zhou Chaorui argued back and forth without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Jia Jichun, however, submitted a memorial in the consort-attendant's defense, and he and Zhou Chaorui quarreled on without end.

sentences.zh: 帝复降敕曰：「九月一日，皇考賓天，大臣入宮哭臨畢，因請朝見。

translations.literal: The emperor again issued an edict saying: "On the first day of the ninth month, my late father departed this life. After the ministers entered the palace to mourn and perform the vigil, they requested an audience."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued another edict: "On the first day of the ninth month my late father passed away. After the ministers entered the palace to mourn, they asked to receive me in audience."

sentences.zh: 選侍阻朕暖閣，司禮監官固請，乃得出。

translations.literal: The consort-attendant blocked me in the warm pavilion. Officials of the Directorate of Ceremonies insisted repeatedly, and only then was I able to come out.
translations.idiomatic: The consort-attendant kept me in the warm pavilion. Only when the eunuchs of the Directorate of Ceremonies pressed again and again was I allowed to emerge.

sentences.zh: 既許复悔，又使李進忠等再三趣回。

translations.literal: Having agreed, she then regretted it and again sent Li Jinzhong and others repeatedly to urge me back.
translations.idiomatic: She consented, then changed her mind, and sent Li Jinzhong and others time after time to bring me back.

sentences.zh: 及朕至乾清丹陛，進忠等猶牽朕衣不釋。

translations.literal: When I reached the red steps of the Palace of Heavenly Purity, Jinzhong and the others still held my robes and would not release them.
translations.idiomatic: Even when I reached the vermilion steps of the Palace of Heavenly Purity, Jinzhong and his men still clutched my robes and would not let go.

sentences.zh: 甫至前宮門，又數數遣人令朕還，毋御文華殿也。

translations.literal: Just as I reached the front palace gate, again and again they sent people ordering me to return and not to ascend the Wenhua Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Hardly had I reached the outer palace gate when messengers were sent again and again telling me to go back and not proceed to the Wenhua Hall.

sentences.zh: 此諸臣所目睹。

translations.literal: This the ministers witnessed with their own eyes.
translations.idiomatic: This the ministers saw with their own eyes.

sentences.zh: 察選侍行事，明欲要挾朕躬，垂簾聽政。

translations.literal: Observing the consort-attendant's conduct, it is clear she wished to hold my person hostage and hold court from behind the curtain.
translations.idiomatic: From the consort-attendant's actions it is plain she meant to seize control of my person and rule from behind the curtain.

sentences.zh: 朕蒙皇考令選侍撫視，飲膳衣服皆皇祖、皇考賜也。

translations.literal: I received my late father's command that the consort-attendant should care for me; food, drink, and clothing were all gifts from my imperial grandfather and late father.
translations.idiomatic: My late father had entrusted me to the consort-attendant's care; my food, drink, and clothing were all gifts from my grandfather and father.

sentences.zh: 選侍侮慢凌虐，朕晝夜涕泣。

translations.literal: The consort-attendant treated me with contempt and cruelty; day and night I wept.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the consort-attendant treated me with contempt and cruelty, and day and night I wept.

sentences.zh: 皇考自知其誤，時加勸慰。

translations.literal: My late father knew himself to have erred and often offered encouragement and consolation.
translations.idiomatic: My late father recognized his mistake and often tried to comfort me.

sentences.zh: 若避宮不早，則爪牙成列，朕且不知若何矣。

translations.literal: If I had not left the palace early, her minions would have lined up in ranks, and I would not have known what would become of me.
translations.idiomatic: Had I not left the palace in time, her minions would have gathered in force, and God knows what would have become of me.

sentences.zh: 選侍因毆崩聖母，自忖有罪，每使宮人竊伺，不令朕與聖母舊侍言，有輒捕去。

translations.literal: Because the consort-attendant had beaten the sacred mother to death, she reckoned herself guilty; she constantly had palace women spy secretly, not allowing me to speak with the sacred mother's former attendants—whoever did so was seized and taken away.
translations.idiomatic: Having beaten the empress dowager to death, the consort-attendant knew herself guilty; she posted palace women to spy on me and forbade me to speak with the empress dowager's old attendants—any who did were seized at once.

sentences.zh: 朕之苦衷，外廷豈能盡悉。

translations.literal: The depths of my suffering—how could the outer court fully know them?
translations.idiomatic: The court outside could hardly know the full measure of my suffering.

sentences.zh: 乃諸臣不念聖母，惟黨選侍，妄生謗議，輕重失倫，理法焉在！

translations.literal: Yet you ministers, not remembering the sacred mother, only sided with the consort-attendant, recklessly stirring up slander—right and rank overturned; where is principle and law!
translations.idiomatic: Yet you ministers, forgetting the empress dowager, took the consort-attendant's side instead, spreading reckless slander until rank and justice were overturned. Where was principle? Where was law?

sentences.zh: 朕今停選侍封號，以慰聖母在天之靈；

translations.literal: I now suspend the consort-attendant's title and rank, to comfort the spirit of the sacred mother in Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: I now withhold the consort-attendant's title and honors, to console the empress dowager's spirit in Heaven;

sentences.zh: 厚養選侍及皇八妹，以敬遵皇考之意。

translations.literal: I shall generously provide for the consort-attendant and my eighth imperial sister, in respectful fulfillment of my late father's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I shall provide generously for the consort-attendant and my eighth imperial sister, in dutiful fulfillment of my late father's wishes.

sentences.zh: 爾諸臣可以仰體朕心矣。

translations.literal: You ministers may thereby comprehend my heart.
translations.idiomatic: You ministers should understand my heart in this.

sentences.zh: 」已，复屢旨詰責繼春，繼春遂削籍去。

translations.literal: After this, edicts repeatedly rebuked Jichun, and Jichun was thereupon stripped of his register and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward repeated edicts censured Jichun, and he was stripped of his official status and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 是時，熹宗初即位，委任司禮太監王安，故敕諭如此。

translations.literal: At this time, when Xizong had just taken the throne, he entrusted Eunuch-Director Wang An of the Directorate of Ceremonies, hence the edicts and instructions were thus.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Xizong had just ascended the throne and relied on Eunuch-Director Wang An of the Directorate of Ceremonies; hence these edicts took the form they did.

sentences.zh: 久之，魏忠賢亂政。

translations.literal: After a long while, Wei Zhongxian threw the government into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: In time Wei Zhongxian came to dominate and corrupt the government.

sentences.zh: 四年封選侍為康妃。

translations.literal: In the fourth year she was granted the title Lady of Imperial Favor Kang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the consort-attendant was ennobled as Lady of Imperial Favor Kang.

sentences.zh: 五年修《三朝要典》，漣、光斗等皆得罪死，復召繼春，與前旨大異矣。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the Three Dynasties Essentials was compiled; Lian, Guangdou, and others all met with punishment and death. Jichun was recalled, greatly at odds with the earlier edicts.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the Three Dynasties Essentials was compiled; Yang Lian, Zuo Guangdou, and others were condemned and executed. Jichun was recalled—a far cry from the earlier edicts.

sentences.zh: 久之，始卒。

translations.literal: After a long while, she finally died.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward she died at last.

sentences.zh: 莊妃李氏，即所稱東李者也。

translations.literal: Lady of Imperial Favor Zhuang Li was the one called Eastern Li.
translations.idiomatic: Lady of Imperial Favor Zhuang Li was the woman known as Eastern Li.

sentences.zh: 仁慈寡言笑，位居西李前，而寵不及。

translations.literal: Kind and forbearing, she spoke and laughed little; her rank preceded Western Li's, yet she did not enjoy equal favor.
translations.idiomatic: Gentle and reserved, she seldom spoke or laughed. Her rank preceded Western Li's, yet she never won comparable favor.

sentences.zh: 莊烈帝幼失母，育於西李。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuanglie lost his mother in youth and was raised by Western Li.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhuanglie lost his mother young and was raised by Western Li.

sentences.zh: 既而西李生女，光宗改命東李撫視。

translations.literal: Later Western Li bore a daughter, and Guangzong changed the order and had Eastern Li care for him.
translations.idiomatic: When Western Li later bore a daughter, Guangzong transferred the young prince to Eastern Li's care.

sentences.zh: 天啟元年二月封莊妃。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Tianqi she was ennobled as Lady of Imperial Favor Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Tianqi 1 she was granted the title Lady of Imperial Favor Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 魏忠賢、客氏用事，惡妃持正，宮中禮數多被裁損，憤鬱薨。

translations.literal: When Wei Zhongxian and Madame Ke held power, they hated the lady for her upright conduct; many of her palace honors were cut back, and she died of indignant grief.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wei Zhongxian and Madame Ke, who resented her integrity, many of her ceremonial honors in the palace were stripped away, and she died of wounded pride.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，詔賜妃弟成楝田產。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongzhen, an edict granted the lady's younger brother Cheng Dong fields and estates.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chongzhen reign, an edict granted her younger brother Cheng Dong fields and estates.

sentences.zh: 選侍趙氏者，光宗時，未有封號。

translations.literal: Consort-attendant Zhao—in Guangzong's time she had no title or rank.
translations.idiomatic: Consort-attendant Zhao had held no title during Guangzong's reign.

sentences.zh: 熹宗即位，忠賢、客氏惡之，矯旨賜自盡。

translations.literal: When Xizong took the throne, Zhongxian and Madame Ke hated her and forged an edict granting her death by her own hand.
translations.idiomatic: When Xizong ascended the throne, Zhongxian and Madame Ke, who despised her, forged an edict ordering her to take her own life.

sentences.zh: 選侍以光宗賜物列案上，西向禮佛，痛哭自經死。

translations.literal: The consort-attendant set out on the table the gifts Guangzong had given her, bowed toward the west to worship the Buddha, wept bitterly, and hanged herself to death.
translations.idiomatic: She arranged on a table the gifts Guangzong had given her, bowed westward to the Buddha, wept bitterly, and hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 熹宗懿安皇后張氏，祥符人。

translations.literal: Empress Yi'an Zhang of Xizong was a native of Xiangfu.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Yi'an Zhang, consort of Emperor Xizong, was from Xiangfu.

sentences.zh: 父國紀，以女貴，封太康伯。

translations.literal: Her father Guo Ji, because of his daughter's honor, was ennobled as Marquis of Taikang.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Guo Ji was ennobled as Marquis of Taikang when his daughter's elevation brought the family honor.

sentences.zh: 天啟元年四月冊為皇后。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Tianqi she was invested as empress.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Tianqi 1 she was formally invested as empress.

sentences.zh: 性嚴正，數於帝前言客氏、魏忠賢過失。

translations.literal: Her nature was stern and upright; she often spoke before the emperor of the faults of Madame Ke and Wei Zhongxian.
translations.idiomatic: Stern and upright by nature, she often spoke to the emperor of the misconduct of Madame Ke and Wei Zhongxian.

sentences.zh: 嘗召客氏至，欲繩以法。

translations.literal: She once summoned Madame Ke and wished to bind her with the law.
translations.idiomatic: She once summoned Madame Ke, intending to hold her accountable under the law.

sentences.zh: 客、魏交恨，遂誣后非國紀女，幾惑帝聽。

translations.literal: Ke and Wei hated her in turn and then slandered the empress as not Guo Ji's daughter, nearly misleading the emperor's judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Madame Ke and Wei Zhongxian turned on her and falsely claimed the empress was not Guo Ji's daughter, nearly swaying the emperor's belief.

sentences.zh: 三年，后有娠，客、魏盡逐宮人異己者，而以其私人承奉，竟損元子。

translations.literal: In the third year the empress became pregnant. Ke and Wei drove out all palace women who differed from them and had their own people attend her, ultimately harming the heir.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the empress became pregnant. Ke and Wei expelled every palace woman who was not their own and replaced them with their creatures, ultimately costing the heir his life.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗至後宮，后方讀書。

translations.literal: The emperor once came to the rear palace; the empress was reading.
translations.idiomatic: Once when the emperor came to the inner quarters, he found the empress reading.

sentences.zh: 帝問何書。

translations.literal: The emperor asked what book it was.
translations.idiomatic: He asked what she was reading.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「《趙高傳》也。

translations.literal: She replied: "It is the Biography of Zhao Gao."
translations.idiomatic: She answered: "The Biography of Zhao Gao."

sentences.zh: 」帝默然。

translations.literal: The emperor fell silent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said nothing.

sentences.zh: 時宮門有匿名書烈忠賢逆狀者，忠賢疑出國紀及被逐諸臣手。

translations.literal: At the time an anonymous letter at the palace gate denounced Wei Zhongxian's treasonous conduct; Zhongxian suspected it came from Guo Ji and the dismissed ministers.
translations.idiomatic: An anonymous placard then appeared at the palace gate denouncing Wei Zhongxian's treachery; he suspected Guo Ji and the expelled officials were behind it.

sentences.zh: 其黨邵輔忠、孫杰等，欲因此興大獄，盡殺東林諸臣，而藉國紀以搖動中宮，冀事成則立魏良卿女為后。

translations.literal: His faction—Shao Fuzhong, Sun Jie, and others—wished thereby to launch a great case, kill all the Donglin ministers, and by means of Guo Ji shake the inner palace, hoping that if the affair succeeded they could install Wei Liangqing's daughter as empress.
translations.idiomatic: His allies Shao Fuzhong and Sun Jie sought to exploit the affair to launch a sweeping prosecution, wipe out the Donglin faction, and use Guo Ji to undermine the empress, hoping ultimately to install Wei Liangqing's daughter on the throne.

sentences.zh: 順天府丞劉志選偵知之，首上疏劾國紀，御史梁夢環繼之，會有沮者乃已。

translations.literal: Assistant prefect of Shuntian Liu Zhixuan detected this and was first to submit a memorial impeaching Guo Ji; Censor Liang Menghuan followed, and only when someone obstructed it did the affair cease.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhixuan, assistant prefect of Shuntian, learned of the plot and was first to impeach Guo Ji; Censor Liang Menghuan followed suit. Only when others intervened was the scheme halted.

sentences.zh: 及熹宗大漸，折忠賢逆謀、傳位信王者，后力也。

translations.literal: When Xizong was near death, it was through the empress's efforts that Wei Zhongxian's treacherous plot was broken and the throne passed to the Prince of Xin.
translations.idiomatic: When Xizong lay dying, it was the empress who thwarted Wei Zhongxian's conspiracy and ensured the throne passed to the Prince of Xin.

sentences.zh: 莊烈帝上尊號曰「懿安皇后」。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuanglie bestowed the honorific title "Empress Yi'an."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhuanglie honored her with the title Empress Yi'an.

sentences.zh: 十七年三月，李自成陷都城，后自縊。

translations.literal: In the third month of the seventeenth year Li Zicheng seized the capital; the empress hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the seventeenth year, when Li Zicheng took the capital, the empress hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，世祖章皇帝命合葬熹宗陵。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi, the Shizu Emperor ordered her interred jointly in Xizong's tomb.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 1 the Shizu Emperor ordered her buried with Xizong in his mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 裕妃張氏，熹宗妃也。

translations.literal: Lady of Imperial Favor Yu Zhang was a consort of Xizong.
translations.idiomatic: Lady of Imperial Favor Yu Zhang was a consort of Emperor Xizong.

sentences.zh: 性直烈。

translations.literal: Her nature was straightforward and fierce.
translations.idiomatic: She was forthright and unyielding by nature.

sentences.zh: 客、魏恚其異己，幽於別宮，絕其飲食。

translations.literal: Ke and Wei resented her for differing from them; they confined her in a separate palace and cut off her food and drink.
translations.idiomatic: Madame Ke and Wei Zhongxian, resenting her independence, shut her in a separate palace and cut off her food and drink.

sentences.zh: 天雨，妃匍匐飲簷溜而死。

translations.literal: When it rained, the lady crawled to drink water dripping from the eaves and died.
translations.idiomatic: When rain fell, she crawled to drink water from the eaves and died.

sentences.zh: 又慧妃范氏者，生悼懷太子不育，复失寵。

translations.literal: There was also Lady of Imperial Favor Hui Fan, who bore Crown Prince Daohuai but he did not survive; she again lost favor.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Lady of Imperial Favor Hui Fan, who bore Crown Prince Daohuai; when the child did not survive, she fell from favor once more.

sentences.zh: 李成妃侍寢，密為慧妃乞憐。

translations.literal: Lady of Imperial Favor Li Cheng attended the emperor in bed and secretly pleaded on Hui's behalf for mercy.
translations.idiomatic: Lady of Imperial Favor Li Cheng, sharing the emperor's bed, secretly interceded for Lady Fan.

sentences.zh: 客、魏知之怒，亦幽成妃於別宮。

translations.literal: When Ke and Wei learned of it they were angry and also confined Lady Cheng in a separate palace.
translations.idiomatic: Madame Ke and Wei Zhongxian learned of this and, enraged, confined Lady Li Cheng in a separate palace as well.

sentences.zh: 妃預藏食物簷瓦間，閉宮中半月不死，斥為宮人。

translations.literal: The lady had beforehand hidden food between the eaves and tiles; shut in the palace for half a month she did not die, and was demoted to palace woman.
translations.idiomatic: She had hidden food under the eaves; though shut away for half a month she survived, and was demoted to the rank of palace maid.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，皆復位號。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongzhen, all had their titles and ranks restored.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chongzhen reign their titles were all restored.

sentences.zh: 莊烈帝愍皇后周氏，其先蘇州人，徙居大興。

translations.literal: Empress Min Zhou of Emperor Zhuanglie—her ancestors were people of Suzhou who moved and settled in Daxing.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Min Zhou, consort of Emperor Zhuanglie, came from a Suzhou family that had moved to Daxing.

sentences.zh: 天啟中，選入信邸。

translations.literal: During Tianqi she was selected and entered the Prince of Xin's residence.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianqi reign she was chosen to enter the household of the Prince of Xin.

sentences.zh: 時神宗劉昭妃攝太后寶，宮中之政悉禀成於熹宗張皇后。

translations.literal: At the time Empress Zhaohui Liu of Shenzong held the empress dowager's seal in regency; all governance within the palace was entirely submitted to and settled by Xizong's Empress Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Empress Zhaohui Liu of Shenzong held the empress dowager's seal; all inner-palace affairs were decided by Empress Zhang of Xizong.

sentences.zh: 故事：宮中選大婚，一后以二貴人陪；

translations.literal: Precedent: in selecting candidates for the grand wedding in the palace, one empress was accompanied by two noble ladies;
translations.idiomatic: By custom, when the palace selected candidates for an imperial wedding, one empress was chosen with two noble ladies as attendants;

sentences.zh: 中選，則皇太后幕以青紗帕，取金玉跳脫係其臂；

translations.literal: if selected, the empress dowager screened her with a green gauze veil, took a gold and jade armlet, and tied it on her arm;
translations.idiomatic: if a girl was chosen, the empress dowager veiled her with a green gauze scarf and fastened a gold and jade bracelet on her arm;

sentences.zh: 不中，即以年月帖子納淑女袖，侑以銀幣遣還。

translations.literal: if not selected, a slip with the year and month was placed in the maiden's sleeve, and she was sent back with silver coins as a gift.
translations.idiomatic: if she was not chosen, a slip noting the date was tucked into her sleeve and she was sent home with a gift of silver.

sentences.zh: 懿安疑后弱，昭妃曰：「今雖弱，後必長大。

translations.literal: Yi'an doubted that the empress was frail; Empress Zhaohui said: "Though weak now, she will surely grow tall later."
translations.idiomatic: Empress Yi'an thought the girl too slight; Empress Zhaohui said: "She may be slight now, but she will surely fill out in time."

sentences.zh: 」因冊為信王妃。

translations.literal: Accordingly she was invested as consort of the Prince of Xin.
translations.idiomatic: On that basis she was invested as consort of the Prince of Xin.

sentences.zh: 帝即位，立為皇后。

translations.literal: When the emperor took the throne, she was established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: When he ascended the throne, she was made empress.

sentences.zh: 后性嚴慎。

translations.literal: The empress's nature was strict and cautious.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was strict and self-restrained by nature.

sentences.zh: 嘗以寇急，微言曰：「吾南中尚有一家居。

translations.literal: Once, because bandits were pressing hard, she said softly: "I still have a home in the south."
translations.idiomatic: Once, with rebels pressing hard, she said quietly: "We still have a home in the south."

sentences.zh: 」帝問之，遂不語，蓋意在南遷也。

translations.literal: The emperor asked about it; she then said nothing—presumably her meaning was relocation to the south.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor pressed her, she fell silent; she had evidently been thinking of flight to the south.

sentences.zh: 至他政事，則未嘗預。

translations.literal: As for other state affairs, she never participated.
translations.idiomatic: In other matters of government she never intervened.

sentences.zh: 田貴妃有寵而驕，后裁之以禮。

translations.literal: Consort Tian was favored and arrogant; the empress restrained her with ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Tian, favored and imperious, was held in check by the empress through strict observance of ritual.

sentences.zh: 歲元日，寒甚，田妃來朝，翟車止廡下。

translations.literal: On New Year's Day of the year, the cold was severe; when Consort Tian came to pay respects, her carriage halted beneath the corridor.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day the cold was bitter. When Consort Tian came to court, her carriage was halted beneath the corridor.

sentences.zh: 后良久方御坐，受其拜，拜已遽下，無他言。

translations.literal: The empress only after a long while took her seat, received her bow, and as soon as the bow was done hurried down—no other words.
translations.idiomatic: The empress waited a long time before taking her seat, accepted the bow, and then immediately stepped down without another word.

sentences.zh: 而袁貴妃之朝也，相見甚歡，語移時。

translations.literal: But when Consort Yuan came to pay respects, they met with great pleasure and spoke for a long while.
translations.idiomatic: When Consort Yuan came to court, by contrast, they greeted each other warmly and talked at length.

sentences.zh: 田妃聞而大恨，向帝泣。

translations.literal: Consort Tian heard of this and hated it greatly; she wept before the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Tian heard of this and was bitterly resentful; she wept before the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗在交泰殿與后語不合，推后僕地，后憤不食。

translations.literal: Once the emperor was in the Jiaotai Hall speaking with the empress when they disagreed; he pushed the empress so she fell to the ground. The empress, angered, refused to eat.
translations.idiomatic: Once in the Jiaotai Hall the emperor quarreled with the empress and shoved her to the floor. In her anger she refused to eat.

sentences.zh: 帝悔，使中使持貂裀賜后，且問起居。

translations.literal: The emperor regretted it and sent a palace envoy bearing a sable rug as a gift to the empress, and also inquired after her health.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor repented and sent a palace envoy with a sable rug as a gift, asking after her health.

sentences.zh: 妃尋以過斥居啟祥宮，三月不召。

translations.literal: Soon the consort, because of a fault, was reprimanded and lodged in the Qixiang Palace; for three months she was not summoned.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Tian was soon banished to the Qixiang Palace for some offense and went uncalled for three months.

sentences.zh: 一日，后侍帝於永和門看花，請召妃。

translations.literal: One day, as the empress attended the emperor viewing flowers at the Yonghe Gate, she asked that the consort be summoned.
translations.idiomatic: One day, while attending the emperor at the Yonghe Gate to view the flowers, the empress asked that Consort Tian be summoned.

sentences.zh: 帝不應。

translations.literal: The emperor did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not agree.

sentences.zh: 后遽令以車迎之，乃相見如初。

translations.literal: The empress at once ordered a carriage to fetch her, and they met again as before.
translations.idiomatic: The empress immediately sent a carriage for her, and they were reconciled as before.

sentences.zh: 帝以寇亂茹蔬。

translations.literal: Because of the rebel turmoil the emperor ate only vegetables.
translations.idiomatic: With rebels ravaging the realm, the emperor lived on vegetables alone.

sentences.zh: 后見帝容體日瘁，具饌將進，而瀛國夫人奏適至，曰：「夜夢孝純太后歸，語帝瘁而泣，且曰：『為我語帝，食毋過苦。

translations.literal: The empress, seeing the emperor's frame daily more wasted, prepared a meal to bring in; just then a memorial from the Lady of Ying arrived, saying: "Last night I dreamed that Empress Dowager Xiaochun returned, spoke of the emperor's wasting and wept, and also said: 'Tell the emperor for me: let his food not be too austere.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the emperor grow thinner day by day, the empress prepared a meal to bring him; just then a memorial arrived from the Lady of Ying: "I dreamed last night that Empress Dowager Xiaochun returned, spoke of the emperor's wasting away and wept, saying, 'Tell the emperor for me: do not eat too sparingly.

sentences.zh: 』」帝持奏入宮，后適進饌。

translations.literal: '" The emperor took the memorial into the palace just as the empress was bringing in the meal.
translations.idiomatic: '" The emperor entered the palace with the memorial just as the empress arrived with the meal.

sentences.zh: 帝追念孝純，且感后意，因出奏示后，再拜舉匕箸，相向而泣，淚盈盈沾案。

translations.literal: The emperor, recalling Xiaochun and moved by the empress's kindness, showed her the memorial; they bowed twice, raised chopsticks, wept facing each other, and tears brimmed over onto the table.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by thoughts of Xiaochun and the empress's care, he showed her the memorial; they bowed, raised their chopsticks, and wept face to face until tears brimmed over the table.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十七年三月十八日暝，都城陷，帝泣語后曰：「大事去矣。

translations.literal: At dusk on the eighteenth day of the third month of the seventeenth year of Chongzhen, the capital fell; weeping, the emperor said to the empress: "The great affair is lost.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk on the eighteenth day of the third month of the seventeenth year of Chongzhen the capital fell; weeping, the emperor told the empress: "All is lost.

sentences.zh: 」后頓首曰：「妾事陛下十有八年，卒不聽一語，至有今日。

translations.literal: " The empress kowtowed and said: "Your servant has attended Your Majesty for eighteen years, yet in the end not one word was heeded, until we have come to this day.
translations.idiomatic: " The empress kowtowed and said: "I have served Your Majesty eighteen years, yet you would not heed a single word of mine—and so we have come to this.

sentences.zh: 」乃撫太子、二王慟哭，遣之出宮。

translations.literal: " She then embraced the crown prince and the two princes and wept bitterly, sending them out of the palace.
translations.idiomatic: " She embraced the crown prince and the two princes, wept bitterly, and sent them from the palace.

sentences.zh: 帝令后自裁。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the empress to take her own life.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the empress to kill herself.

sentences.zh: 后入室闔戶，宮人出奏，猶云「皇后領旨」。

translations.literal: The empress entered her chamber and closed the door; a palace woman came out to report, still saying "The empress has received the decree."
translations.idiomatic: The empress went to her chamber and closed the door; a palace woman came out to report that the empress had received the decree.

sentences.zh: 后遂先帝崩。

translations.literal: The empress then died before the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The empress died before the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝又命袁貴妃自縊，系絕，久之蘇。

translations.literal: The emperor also ordered Consort Yuan to hang herself; the cord broke, and after a long while she revived.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also ordered Consort Yuan to hang herself; the cord snapped, and after a long while she revived.

sentences.zh: 帝拔劍斫其肩，又斫所御妃嬪數人，袁妃卒不殊。

translations.literal: The emperor drew his sword and hacked her shoulder, then hacked several of the consorts he favored; Consort Yuan in the end was not killed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor drew his sword and struck her shoulder, then struck down several favored consorts; Consort Yuan alone survived.

sentences.zh: 世祖章皇帝定鼎，諡后曰「莊烈愍皇后」，與帝同葬田貴妃寢園，名曰「思陵」。

translations.literal: When the Shizu Zhang Emperor established the dynasty, the empress was given the posthumous title "Empress Zhuanglie Min" and buried with the emperor in Consort Tian's mausoleum garden, named "Siling."
translations.idiomatic: When the Shizu Zhang Emperor took the throne, she was posthumously titled Empress Zhuanglie Min and buried with the emperor in Consort Tian's mausoleum precinct, called Siling.

sentences.zh: 下所司給袁妃居宅，贍養終其身。

translations.literal: Orders were issued to the relevant offices to provide Consort Yuan with a residence and support her for life.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities were ordered to provide Consort Yuan with a residence and maintain her for life.

sentences.zh: 有宮人魏氏者，當賊入宮，大呼曰：「我輩必遭賊污，有志者早為計。

translations.literal: There was a palace woman of the Wei clan; when the rebels entered the palace she cried out: "We shall surely be defiled by the rebels—let those with resolve act early.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels entered the palace, a palace woman surnamed Wei cried out: "We shall surely be defiled by the rebels—let those with resolve act now.

sentences.zh: 」遂躍入御河死，頃間從死者一二百人。

translations.literal: " She then leaped into the Imperial River and died; within moments one or two hundred followed her to death.
translations.idiomatic: " She leaped into the Imperial River and died; within moments one or two hundred followed.

sentences.zh: 宮人費氏，年十六，自投眢井中。

translations.literal: The palace woman Fei, aged sixteen, threw herself into a dry well.
translations.idiomatic: A palace woman named Fei, sixteen years old, threw herself into a dry well.

sentences.zh: 賊鉤出，見其姿容，爭奪之。

translations.literal: The rebels hooked her out, saw her beauty, and fought over her.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fished her out, saw her beauty, and fought over her.

sentences.zh: 費氏紿曰：「我長公主也。

translations.literal: Fei deceived them, saying: "I am the eldest princess.
translations.idiomatic: Fei deceived them: "I am the eldest princess.

sentences.zh: 」群賊不敢逼，擁見李自成。

translations.literal: " The band of rebels did not dare force her and escorted her to Li Zicheng.
translations.idiomatic: " The rebels did not dare molest her and escorted her to Li Zicheng.

sentences.zh: 自成命中官審視之，非是，以賞部校羅某者。

translations.literal: Zicheng ordered palace eunuchs to examine her; she was not genuine, and he gave her as a reward to a certain company commander Luo.
translations.idiomatic: Zicheng had palace eunuchs examine her; she was not the princess, and he gave her as a reward to a company commander named Luo.

sentences.zh: 費氏复紿羅曰：「我實天潢，義難苟合，將軍宜擇吉成禮。

translations.literal: Fei again deceived Luo, saying: "I am truly of the imperial line; righteousness forbids casual union—the general should choose an auspicious day for the full rites.
translations.idiomatic: Fei deceived Luo again: "I am truly of the imperial blood; I cannot yield to force—General, choose an auspicious day for the wedding rites.

sentences.zh: 」羅喜，置酒極歡。

translations.literal: " Luo was delighted and set out wine for great revelry.
translations.idiomatic: " Luo was delighted and set out wine for a great feast.

sentences.zh: 費氏懷利刃，俟羅醉，斷其喉立死。

translations.literal: Fei concealed a sharp blade; when Luo was drunk she cut his throat and he died at once.
translations.idiomatic: Fei hid a sharp blade; when Luo was drunk she cut his throat and killed him instantly.

sentences.zh: 因自詫曰：「我一弱女子，殺一賊帥足矣。

translations.literal: She then said to herself in wonder: "I, a weak woman, have killed one rebel chieftain—that is enough.
translations.idiomatic: She said to herself: "I, a weak woman, have killed one rebel chieftain—that is enough.

sentences.zh: 」遂自刎死。

translations.literal: " She then cut her own throat and died.
translations.idiomatic: " She then cut her own throat and died.

sentences.zh: 自成聞大驚，令收葬之。

translations.literal: Zicheng, hearing of this, was greatly shocked and ordered her gathered and buried.
translations.idiomatic: Zicheng, hearing of it, was greatly shocked and ordered her properly buried.

sentences.zh: 恭淑貴妃田氏，陝西人，后家揚州。

translations.literal: Imperial Noble Consort Gongshu Tian was a native of Shaanxi; the empress's family was from Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Noble Consort Gongshu Tian came from Shaanxi; the empress's family was from Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 父弘遇以女貴，官左都督，好佚遊，為輕俠。

translations.literal: Her father Hongyu, because of his daughter's rank, held the post of Left Chief Commander; he loved dissolute travel and was known as a light ruffian.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Hongyu, elevated by his daughter's rank to Left Chief Commander, loved dissolute pleasures and was known as a swaggering rake.

sentences.zh: 妃生而纖妍，性寡言，多才藝，侍莊烈帝於信邸。

translations.literal: The consort was born slender and lovely, taciturn by nature, skilled in many arts, and attended the Chonglie Emperor at the Prince of Xin's residence.
translations.idiomatic: She was born slender and beautiful, quiet by nature, accomplished in many arts, and served the Chongzhen Emperor when he was Prince of Xin.

sentences.zh: 崇禎元年封禮妃，進皇貴妃。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongzhen she was enfeoffed as Li consort and advanced to imperial noble consort.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chongzhen she was made Li consort and then promoted to imperial noble consort.

sentences.zh: 宮中有夾道，暑月駕行幸，御蓋行日中。

translations.literal: Within the palace there was a covered passage; in summer months when the imperial carriage went on progress, the imperial canopy traveled in the midday sun.
translations.idiomatic: The palace had covered passages; in summer when the emperor traveled in his carriage, the imperial canopy still passed through the midday sun.

sentences.zh: 妃命作蘧篨覆之，從者皆得休息。

translations.literal: The consort ordered rush matting spread over it so that all who followed could rest.
translations.idiomatic: She ordered rush matting spread overhead so that all who followed could rest in the shade.

sentences.zh: 又易小黃門之舁輿者以宮婢。

translations.literal: She also replaced the junior eunuchs who bore the sedan with palace maids.
translations.idiomatic: She also replaced the junior eunuchs who carried the sedan with palace women.

sentences.zh: 帝聞，以為知禮。

translations.literal: The emperor heard of this and considered her knowledgeable in ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard of this and judged her observant of propriety.

sentences.zh: 嘗有過，謫別宮省愆。

translations.literal: Once, for a fault, she was banished to a separate palace to reflect on her errors.
translations.idiomatic: Once, for some offense, she was sent to a separate palace to reflect on her faults.

sentences.zh: 所生皇五子，​​薨於別宮，妃遂病。

translations.literal: The fifth imperial son she bore died in the separate palace, and the consort then fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: The fifth imperial son she bore died in the separate palace, and she fell ill.

sentences.zh: 十五年七月薨。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fifteenth year she died.
translations.idiomatic: She died in the seventh month of the fifteenth year.

sentences.zh: 諡恭淑端惠靜懷皇貴妃，葬昌平天壽山，即思陵也。

translations.literal: She was given the posthumous title Imperial Noble Consort Gongshu Duanhui Jinghuai and buried at Tianshou Mountain in Changping—that is, Siling.
translations.idiomatic: She received the posthumous title Imperial Noble Consort Gongshu Duanhui Jinghuai and was buried at Tianshou Mountain in Changping—the site of Siling.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：高皇后從太祖備歷艱難，贊成大業，母儀天下，慈德昭彰。

translations.literal: The eulogy says: Empress Gao followed the Founding Emperor through every hardship, aided the completion of the great enterprise, embodied the motherly model for all under Heaven, and her benevolent virtue shone forth.
translations.idiomatic: The eulogy reads: Empress Gao followed the Founding Emperor through every hardship, helped bring the great enterprise to completion, set the maternal standard for the realm, and her benevolence shone forth.

sentences.zh: 繼以文皇后仁孝寬和，化行宮壼，後世承其遺範，內治肅雍。

translations.literal: She was succeeded by Empress Wen, benevolent, filial, generous, and harmonious; her transforming influence prevailed within the palace, and later generations inherited her legacy, so that inner governance was solemn and harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wen followed—benevolent, filial, generous, and harmonious; her influence transformed the inner palace, and later generations inherited her example, so that domestic governance was solemn and orderly.

sentences.zh: 論者稱有明家法，遠過漢、唐，信不誣矣。

translations.literal: Commentators say that the Ming household regulations far surpassed those of Han and Tang—this is truly no empty boast.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators hold that Ming domestic discipline far surpassed Han and Tang—it was no empty boast.

sentences.zh: 萬、鄭兩貴妃，亦非有陰鷙之謀、干政奪嫡之事，徒以恃寵溺愛，遂滋謗訕。

translations.literal: The two noble consorts Wan and Zheng likewise had no secret, sinister plots or affairs of meddling in government and seizing the succession; they merely, through relying on favor and doting affection, gave rise to slander.
translations.idiomatic: The noble consorts Wan and Zheng likewise plotted no dark schemes and meddled not in succession politics; they merely, through excessive favor, drew slander upon themselves.

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：「閒有家，悔亡。

translations.literal: The Book of Changes says: "Regulate the household, and remorse disappears.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says: "Regulate the household, and remorse disappears.

sentences.zh: 」苟越其閒，悔將無及。

translations.literal: " If one oversteps those bounds, remorse will be beyond remedy.
translations.idiomatic: " Overstep those bounds, and remorse will come too late.

sentences.zh: 聖人之垂戒遠矣哉。

translations.literal: How far-reaching is the sage's admonition!
translations.idiomatic: How far-reaching the sage's warning!
